subject: Biology

question_english: Where is life widely believed to have originated, and what alternative view do some researchers hold?
question_hinglish: Life ki shuruaat kahan hui thi, aur kuch researchers iske baare mein alag kya sochte hain?
answer_english: Life is widely believed to have originated in water. Some researchers suggest that it may have begun in small water pools with changing environmental conditions, such as hot springs, rather than in the oceans.
answer_hinglish: Zyada tar scientists maante hain ki life paani mein shuru hui thi. Lekin kuch researchers kehte hain ki shayad yeh oceans mein nahi, balki chhote water pools mein shuru hui jahan conditions badalti rehti thi, jaise hot springs.
ncert_context: The scientific community broadly agrees that life first appeared in water. However, some researchers argue that the oceans may not have been the starting point. Instead, they believe small water pools with fluctuating conditions, like hot springs, offered a better setting. Such environments experience changes in temperature and chemistry that could have encouraged the formation of early biological molecules.

question_english: Why are the hot springs of Puga Valley in Ladakh important for understanding the origin of life?
question_hinglish: Ladakh ki Puga Valley ke hot springs life ki origin samajhne ke liye important kyun hain?
answer_english: The hot springs of Puga Valley maintain temperatures close to the boiling point of water even in a cold climate. These conditions resemble those of the early Earth about 3.5 billion years ago, so studying them helps scientists understand how early life may have formed.
answer_hinglish: Puga Valley ke hot springs ka temperature thandi jagah hone ke baawajood lagbhag boiling point tak rehta hai. Yeh conditions early Earth jaisi hain, around 3.5 billion saal pehle wali. Isliye inhe study karke scientists samajh sakte hain ki pehli life kaise bani hogi.
ncert_context: Puga Valley in Ladakh has hot springs whose water stays nearly at boiling point despite the freezing climate around them. Scientists consider these conditions similar to the environment of the early Earth roughly 3.5 billion years ago. Because of this, such hot springs act like natural laboratories where researchers can study the kind of setting in which the first cells may have arisen.

question_english: What are thermophiles?
question_hinglish: Thermophiles kya hote hain?
answer_english: Thermophiles are heat-loving, unicellular bacteria that live in extremely hot environments such as the hot springs of Puga Valley in Ladakh.
answer_hinglish: Thermophiles woh unicellular bacteria hain jinhe garmi pasand hai. Yeh bahut hot jagahon mein rehte hain, jaise Ladakh ki Puga Valley ke hot springs.
ncert_context: Some organisms thrive in conditions that would kill most living things. In the hot springs of Puga Valley, where water is nearly boiling, the main inhabitants are bacteria that love heat. These single-celled organisms are called thermophiles. Their ability to survive extreme temperatures makes them interesting to scientists who study what life on the early Earth may have been like.

subject: Biology

question_english: How might the calcium carbonate deposits around hot springs have helped in the formation of the first cells?
question_hinglish: Hot springs ke aas-paas jo calcium carbonate deposits bante hain, unhone pehle cells banne mein kaise help ki hogi?
answer_english: Scientists from the Birbal Sahni Institute of Palaeosciences found that calcium carbonate forms rapidly around hot springs. These deposits may have shielded early organic molecules from harmful radiation and extreme conditions, and may also have helped form the first protective membrane, the barrier that defines a cell.
answer_hinglish: Birbal Sahni Institute ke scientists ne dekha ki hot springs ke paas calcium carbonate bahut jaldi jam jaata hai. Yeh deposits early organic molecules ko harmful radiation aur extreme conditions se bachate honge. Saath hi, shayad inhone pehli protective membrane banne mein bhi help ki, jo ek cell ki boundary define karti hai.
ncert_context: Researchers from the Birbal Sahni Institute of Palaeosciences, Lucknow, studied the Puga Valley hot springs and observed that calcium carbonate deposits formed quickly around them. Early organic molecules would have been fragile and easily damaged by radiation and harsh surroundings. A protective covering could have kept them safe, and such deposits may even have contributed to forming the first membrane that separated a cell from its environment.

question_english: Differentiate between unicellular and multicellular organisms with examples.
question_hinglish: Unicellular aur multicellular organisms mein kya difference hai? Examples ke saath batao.
answer_english: Unicellular organisms consist of only one cell that carries out all life functions, for example bacteria and yeast. Multicellular organisms are made up of millions of cells that work together, for example plants, fish, birds and humans.
answer_hinglish: Unicellular organisms mein sirf ek hi cell hota hai jo saare life functions khud karta hai, jaise bacteria aur yeast. Multicellular organisms mein millions of cells hote hain jo milkar kaam karte hain, jaise plants, fish, birds aur humans.
ncert_context: All living organisms are made of cells, but the number of cells varies greatly. Some organisms, like bacteria and yeast, are just a single cell that performs every task needed for survival. Others, such as plants, fish, birds and humans, contain millions of cells. In these multicellular organisms, cells divide the work among themselves and cooperate to keep the organism alive.

question_english: Describe the levels of organisation from cells to organ systems with an example.
question_hinglish: Cells se lekar organ systems tak levels of organisation kaise hote hain? Ek example do.
answer_english: A group of similar cells performing similar functions forms a tissue. Different tissues are organised to form an organ, and several organs work together to form an organ system. For example, the nasal pores, nasal cavity, trachea and lungs together form the respiratory system.
answer_hinglish: Similar cells jo same kaam karte hain, milkar tissue banate hain. Alag-alag tissues milkar ek organ banate hain, aur kai organs milkar organ system banate hain. Jaise nasal pores, nasal cavity, trachea aur lungs milkar respiratory system banate hain.
ncert_context: In multicellular organisms, cells are arranged in a hierarchy. Similar cells that do the same job group together as tissues. Different tissues combine to make an organ, which performs a particular function. Several organs then work as a team to form an organ system. The respiratory system, for instance, includes the nasal pores, nasal cavity, trachea and lungs, all working together for breathing.

subject: Biology
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life
question_english: Why is the cell called the fundamental unit of structure and function in living organisms?
question_hinglish: Cell ko living organisms ki fundamental unit of structure aur function kyun kehte hain?
answer_english: The cell is called the fundamental unit because all living organisms are made of cells, and even when cells are organised into tissues, organs and organ systems, every life activity ultimately takes place inside cells. It is the basic level at which life exists.
answer_hinglish: Kyunki har living organism cells se hi bana hota hai. Chahe cells tissues, organs ya organ systems mein organise ho jaayein, saari life activities finally cells ke andar hi hoti hain. Life jis basic level pe exist karti hai, woh cell hi hai.
ncert_context: Whether an organism is a single bacterium or a human being, its body is built from cells. In complex organisms, cells are organised into tissues, organs and organ systems, yet each of these depends on the work done by individual cells. The cell is the smallest level at which all the properties of life can be seen, which is why it is regarded as the basic unit of structure and function.

question_english: What is meant by the limit of resolution of the human eye?
question_hinglish: Human eye ka limit of resolution kya hota hai?
answer_english: The limit of resolution of the human eye is the smallest distance at which two close points can still be seen as separate. For the human eye, viewed from about 25 cm, this limit is about 0.1 mm.
answer_hinglish: Limit of resolution woh minimum distance hai jis pe do paas-paas ke points ko hum alag-alag dekh paate hain. Human eye ke liye, lagbhag 25 cm ki doori se dekhne pe, yeh limit about 0.1 mm hoti hai.
ncert_context: Imagine two dots on paper being moved closer and closer. At some point, they can no longer be told apart and appear as one dot. The minimum separation at which two points are seen as distinct is called the limit of resolution. When viewed from about 25 cm, the near point of the human eye, this limit is roughly 0.1 mm, which is why most cells cannot be seen without help.

question_english: Why can most cells not be seen with the unaided eye?
question_hinglish: Zyada tar cells naked eye se dikhte kyun nahi hain?
answer_english: Most cells are much smaller than 0.1 mm, which is the limit of resolution of the human eye. Since objects smaller than this cannot be distinguished by the naked eye, cells must be observed using a microscope.
answer_hinglish: Kyunki zyada tar cells 0.1 mm se bhi chhote hote hain, aur 0.1 mm hi human eye ka limit of resolution hai. Isse chhoti cheezein aankh alag se pehchaan nahi paati, isliye cells dekhne ke liye microscope chahiye.
ncert_context: When viewed from about 25 cm, the near point of the human eye, two points must be about 0.1 mm apart to be seen as distinct. This is the limit of resolution of the human eye. Most plant and animal cells are smaller than this, around 10 to 100 µm, and bacteria are even smaller. A cell is therefore usually too small to be seen by the unaided eye, so microscopes are used.

subject: Biology
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life
question_english: The diameter of the field of view of a microscope is 5 mm, and 25 onion peel cells are seen along this diameter. Estimate the size of one onion cell.
question_hinglish: Microscope ke field of view ka diameter 5 mm hai aur us diameter pe 25 onion peel cells dikh rahe hain. Ek onion cell ka size kitna hoga?
answer_english:
Given: diameter of field = 5 mm, number of cells = 25.
Step 1: Convert to micrometres: 5 mm x 1000 = 5000 µm.
Step 2: Size of one cell = diameter / number of cells = 5000 µm / 25 = 200 µm.
The estimated size of one onion peel cell is 200 µm.
answer_hinglish:
Given: field ka diameter = 5 mm, cells = 25.
Step 1: Pehle micrometre mein convert karo: 5 mm x 1000 = 5000 µm.
Step 2: Ek cell ka size = diameter / cells ki number = 5000 µm / 25 = 200 µm.
Toh ek onion peel cell ka size lagbhag 200 µm hai.
ncert_context: We can estimate the size of a cell using a microscope and a transparent ruler. First, the diameter of the circular field of view is measured in millimetres and converted to micrometres, since 1 mm equals 1000 µm. Then an onion peel slide is placed on the stage and the cells lying in a straight line across the diameter are counted. Dividing the diameter by the number of cells gives the size of each cell.

subject: Biology

question_english: If the eyepiece of a microscope has a magnifying power of 10X and the objective lens has 40X, what is the total magnification? How large will a 200 µm cell appear?
question_hinglish: Agar eyepiece ka magnifying power 10X hai aur objective lens ka 40X, toh total magnification kitna hoga? 200 µm ka cell kitna bada dikhega?
answer_english:
Total magnification = eyepiece power x objective power = 10 x 40 = 400X.
Apparent size = 200 µm x 400 = 80,000 µm = 80 mm.
The cell will appear 400 times larger, that is about 80 mm.
answer_hinglish:

ncert_context: The total magnification of a light microscope is found by multiplying the magnifying power of the eyepiece by that of the objective lens. Switching to a higher-power objective lens increases the total magnification and makes even finer details visible.

question_english: How is an electron microscope different from a light microscope?

answer_hinglish: Light microscope visible light aur lenses use karta hai, jabki electron microscope electrons ki beam use karta hai. Isliye electron microscope bahut zyada magnified images deta hai aur cell ke structures ko nanometre scale tak dikha sakta hai.

Electron microscopes overcome this by using a beam of electrons instead of light. This allows them to produce extremely magnified and clear images, revealing structures as small as a few nanometres, where one nanometre is one-billionth of a metre.

subject: Biology

question_english: What is the cell membrane?
question_hinglish: Cell membrane kya hoti hai?
answer_english: The cell membrane, also called the plasma membrane, is a thin boundary that surrounds a cell and protects its contents. It defines the individuality of the cell and controls the movement of substances in and out.
answer_hinglish: Cell membrane, jise plasma membrane bhi kehte hain, ek patli boundary hai jo cell ko chaaron taraf se gherti hai aur uske contents ko protect karti hai. Yeh cell ki individuality define karti hai aur control karti hai ki kya andar aaye aur kya bahar jaaye.
ncert_context: Every cell is enclosed by a thin boundary known as the cell membrane or plasma membrane. It separates the cell's contents from its surroundings and gives the cell its own identity. All interactions between a cell and its environment, such as taking in nutrients and releasing wastes, happen across this boundary. Even single-celled organisms depend on their membrane to exchange materials and respond to the environment.

question_english: Define osmosis.
question_hinglish: Osmosis ki definition batao.
answer_english: Osmosis is the movement of water through a selectively permeable membrane from a region of more water and less solute (dilute solution) to a region of less water and more solute (concentrated solution), until the concentrations on both sides become equal.
answer_hinglish: Osmosis matlab paani ka selectively permeable membrane ke through movement, us side se jahan paani zyada aur solute kam hai (dilute solution), us side ki taraf jahan paani kam aur solute zyada hai (concentrated solution). Yeh tab tak hota hai jab tak dono taraf ki concentration equal na ho jaaye.
ncert_context: When two solutions of different concentrations are separated by a selectively permeable membrane, water tends to move across it. Water moves from the dilute side, which has more water and less solute, to the concentrated side, which has less water and more solute. This continues until the concentrations become equal. This special kind of diffusion of water is known as osmosis.

question_english: Differentiate between diffusion and osmosis.
question_hinglish: Diffusion aur osmosis mein kya difference hai?
answer_english: Diffusion is the net movement of particles of any substance from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration, and it can occur even without a membrane. Osmosis is specifically the diffusion of water across a selectively permeable membrane.
answer_hinglish: Diffusion mein kisi bhi substance ke particles higher concentration se lower concentration ki taraf move karte hain, aur iske liye membrane zaroori nahi hai. Osmosis specifically paani ka diffusion hai jo selectively permeable membrane ke through hota hai.
ncert_context: Particles of matter naturally spread out and intermix because of differences in their concentrations, called a concentration gradient. A drop of dye spreading in water or a fragrance spreading in air are examples of diffusion, which does not require any membrane. Osmosis is a special case in which only water moves, and it does so across a selectively permeable membrane such as the cell membrane.

question_english: What are isotonic, hypotonic and hypertonic solutions?
question_hinglish: Isotonic, hypotonic aur hypertonic solutions kya hote hain?
answer_english: In an isotonic solution, the solute concentration outside the cell is equal to that inside. In a hypotonic solution, the solute concentration outside is lower than inside, so water enters the cell. In a hypertonic solution, the solute concentration outside is higher than inside, so water leaves the cell.
answer_hinglish: Isotonic solution mein bahar aur cell ke andar solute concentration barabar hoti hai. Hypotonic solution mein bahar solute kam hota hai, toh paani cell ke andar jaata hai. Hypertonic solution mein bahar solute zyada hota hai, toh paani cell se bahar nikalta hai.
ncert_context: The effect of a solution on a cell depends on how its solute concentration compares with that of the cell's interior. If both are equal, there is no net movement of water and the solution is isotonic. If the surrounding solution is more dilute, it is hypotonic and the cell gains water. If the surrounding solution is more concentrated, it is hypertonic and the cell loses water.

question_english: Mung bean seeds that have been soaked in water for 12 hours are kept in a concentrated salt solution. What will happen to them and why?

subject: Biology
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life
question_english: Explain the fluid-mosaic model of the cell membrane.
question_hinglish: Cell membrane ka fluid-mosaic model explain karo.
answer_english: According to the fluid-mosaic model, the membrane has a lipid bilayer with water-attracting heads facing outwards and water-repelling tails facing inwards, with proteins embedded in it. It is fluid because its molecules can move sideways, flip and rotate. It is a mosaic because the molecules are arranged like tiles in a mosaic. The proteins act like gatekeepers that help substances pass through.
answer_hinglish: Fluid-mosaic model ke hisaab se membrane mein ek lipid bilayer hoti hai, jisme water-attracting heads bahar ki taraf aur water-repelling tails andar ki taraf hoti hain, aur iske beech proteins embedded hote hain. Ise fluid isliye kehte hain kyunki molecules sideways move, flip aur rotate kar sakte hain. Mosaic isliye kyunki molecules tiles ki tarah arranged hote hain. Proteins gatekeepers ki tarah substances ko pass hone mein help karte hain.
ncert_context: The structure of the cell membrane is explained by the fluid-mosaic model. The membrane is made of two layers of special fat molecules, forming a lipid bilayer. Their water-attracting heads point outward and water-repelling tails point inward. Various proteins are embedded in this bilayer. The molecules are not fixed; they move sideways, flip and rotate, and their pattern resembles the tiles of a mosaic.

The structure of the cell membrane is explained by the fluid-mosaic model. The membrane is made of two layers of special fat molecules, forming a lipid bilayer. Their water-attracting heads point outward and water-repelling tails point inward. Various proteins are embedded in this bilayer. The molecules are not fixed; they move sideways, flip and rotate, and their pattern resembles the tiles of a mosaic.

Cell membrane ka fluid-mosaic model explain karo.

Answer the question in Hinglish using only the given context.

Fluid-mosaic model ke hisaab se membrane mein ek lipid bilayer hoti hai, jisme water-attracting heads bahar ki taraf aur water-repelling tails andar ki taraf hoti hain, aur iske beech proteins embedded hote hain. Ise fluid isliye kehte hain kyunki molecules sideways move, flip aur rotate kar sakte hain. Mosaic isliye kyunki molecules tiles ki tarah arranged hote hain. Proteins gatekeepers ki tarah substances ko pass hone mein help karte hain.

question_english: What is the role of proteins present in the cell membrane?
question_hinglish: Cell membrane mein jo proteins hote hain unka kya role hai?
answer_english: Proteins in the cell membrane act like gatekeepers. They help specific substances pass across the membrane, controlling what enters and leaves the cell.

By allowing certain substances through and keeping others out, the membrane proteins work much like gatekeepers, helping the cell regulate its internal environment.

subject: Biology
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life
question_english: How does the structure of the cell membrane in the alveoli help in the exchange of gases?
question_hinglish: Alveoli ke cells ki cell membrane ka structure gas exchange mein kaise help karta hai?
answer_english: The cell membrane is extremely thin, about 7 to 10 nm, and selectively permeable. Oxygen and carbon dioxide move across the membranes of alveolar cells by diffusion, from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.
answer_hinglish: Cell membrane bahut patli hoti hai, sirf 7 se 10 nm, aur selectively permeable hoti hai. Oxygen aur carbon dioxide alveoli ke cells ki membranes ke through diffusion se move karte hain, yaani higher concentration se lower concentration ki taraf.
ncert_context: The cell membrane is extremely thin, about 7 to 10 nanometres, and is selectively permeable, allowing some substances to pass while blocking others. Oxygen and carbon dioxide move across the membranes of the alveoli in the lungs. Diffusion is the net movement of particles from a higher to a lower concentration, driven by a concentration gradient, and all cells communicate with their surroundings through the cell membrane.

subject: Biology
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life
question_english: Why do plant cells need a cell wall?
question_hinglish: Plant cells ko cell wall ki zaroorat kyun hoti hai?
answer_english: Plants cannot move from place to place, so they need a rigid structure to withstand environmental stresses like wind and rain. The cell wall provides this rigidity, helps leaves and flowers remain firm and keep their shape, and helps plants stay upright.
answer_hinglish: Plants ek jagah se doosri jagah move nahi kar sakte, isliye unhe wind aur rain jaise stresses jhelne ke liye ek rigid structure chahiye. Cell wall yahi rigidity deti hai, leaves aur flowers ko firm rakhti hai, unka shape maintain karti hai aur plant ko seedha khade rehne mein help karti hai.
ncert_context: Unlike animals, plants generally stay rooted in one place and must face wind, rain and other stresses where they stand. To cope with this, plant cells have an extra covering outside the cell membrane called the cell wall. This rigid layer gives strength and support to the cells, keeps leaves and flowers firm, maintains their shape and allows the plant to stand upright.

Interestingly, the cellulose we eat in plant foods cannot be digested by us but acts as roughage, helping our digestive system work smoothly.

subject: Biology
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life
question_english: Differentiate between the cell membrane and the cell wall on the basis of permeability.
question_hinglish: Permeability ke basis pe cell membrane aur cell wall mein difference batao.
answer_english: The cell membrane is selectively permeable, allowing only certain substances such as water to pass while blocking others like salt and sugar. The cell wall is freely permeable, allowing water and many dissolved minerals to pass through it.
answer_hinglish: Cell membrane selectively permeable hoti hai, yaani sirf kuch substances jaise paani ko jaane deti hai aur salt, sugar jaise substances ko rok deti hai. Cell wall freely permeable hoti hai, isme se paani aur kai dissolved minerals aasani se pass ho jaate hain.
ncert_context: Plant cells have two boundary layers: the inner cell membrane and the outer cell wall. They differ in how they let substances through. The cell membrane is choosy, permitting some molecules to cross and blocking others. The cell wall, though rigid, is permeable and lets water and dissolved minerals pass easily. Working together, both layers help root cells absorb water and nutrients.

question_english: When a Rhoeo leaf peel is placed in concentrated sugar solution, the cell boundary remains the same but the inner contents shrink. Explain this observation.
question_hinglish: Rhoeo leaf peel ko concentrated sugar solution mein rakhne pe cell ki boundary same rehti hai par andar ka content sikud jaata hai. Aisa kyun hota hai?
answer_english: The cells lose water to the concentrated sugar solution by osmosis. However, the rigid cell wall maintains the cell's outer shape, so only the inner contents shrink as the cell membrane pulls away from the cell wall, increasing the space between the two boundaries.
answer_hinglish: Osmosis se cells ka paani concentrated sugar solution mein chala jaata hai. Lekin rigid cell wall cell ka bahar ka shape maintain rakhti hai, isliye sirf andar ka content sikudta hai aur cell membrane cell wall se door khinch jaati hai. Isse dono boundaries ke beech gap badh jaata hai.
ncert_context: When plant cells such as those of a Rhoeo or onion peel are placed in a concentrated sugar solution, water moves out of them by osmosis. Because the cell wall is rigid, the outer outline of the cell does not change. Instead, the cell membrane and the contents inside it shrink and pull away from the wall. This leaves a visible gap between the inner and outer boundaries of the cell.

subject: Biology
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life
question_english: Why do cheek cells shrink considerably in concentrated sugar solution while Rhoeo leaf cells keep their outer shape?
question_hinglish: Concentrated sugar solution mein cheek cells kaafi sikud jaate hain, lekin Rhoeo leaf cells ka bahar ka shape same rehta hai. Aisa kyun?
answer_english: Cheek cells are animal cells and do not have a cell wall, so when they lose water by osmosis the whole cell shrinks. Rhoeo leaf cells have a rigid cell wall that maintains their outer shape, so only their inner contents shrink.
answer_hinglish: Cheek cells animal cells hain aur unme cell wall nahi hoti, isliye osmosis se paani nikalne pe poora cell sikud jaata hai. Rhoeo leaf cells mein rigid cell wall hoti hai jo bahar ka shape maintain rakhti hai, toh sirf andar ka content sikudta hai.
ncert_context: If slides of human cheek cells and Rhoeo leaf peel are both treated with 20 per cent sugar solution, both lose water by osmosis. Yet the results look different under the microscope. Plant cells keep their outline because the cell wall is rigid, and only the contents shrink inside. Animal cells like cheek cells lack a cell wall, so nothing holds their shape and the entire cell shrinks noticeably.

chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life
question_english: Cell X is placed in pure water and swells, while Cell Y is placed in concentrated salt solution and shrinks. Which statement correctly explains this? (i) Salt moved into Cell Y causing it to shrink (ii) Water moved into Cell X and more water moved out of Cell Y than salt entered it (iii) Water moved into Cell X and moved out of Cell Y through the cell membrane (iv) Solute movement caused osmosis in both cells
question_hinglish: Cell X ko pure water mein rakha toh woh phool gaya, aur Cell Y ko concentrated salt solution mein rakha toh woh sikud gaya. Kaun sa statement sahi explanation deta hai? (i) Salt Cell Y mein gaya isliye woh sikuda (ii) Paani Cell X mein gaya aur Cell Y se jitna salt andar aaya usse zyada paani bahar gaya (iii) Paani cell membrane ke through Cell X mein gaya aur Cell Y se bahar gaya (iv) Solute movement ki wajah se dono cells mein osmosis hua
answer_english: The correct option is (iii). Water moved into Cell X from the pure water and moved out of Cell Y into the concentrated salt solution through the selectively permeable cell membrane by osmosis. Salt does not cross the membrane.
answer_hinglish: Sahi option (iii) hai. Osmosis se paani pure water se Cell X ke andar gaya aur Cell Y se concentrated salt solution mein bahar gaya, selectively permeable cell membrane ke through. Salt membrane cross nahi karta.
ncert_context: Osmosis involves only the movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane; the solute, such as salt, does not pass through. Pure water is hypotonic compared to the cell contents, so water enters the cell and it swells. A concentrated salt solution is hypertonic, so water leaves the cell and it shrinks. Explanations that involve salt moving across the membrane are therefore incorrect.

question_english: What are the three basic parts found in most cells?
question_hinglish: Zyada tar cells mein kaun se teen basic parts hote hain?

In addition, the cytoplasm holds several organelles, most of which are visible only with an electron microscope.

question_english: Distinguish between viruses, viroids and prions.
question_hinglish: Viruses, viroids aur prions mein kya difference hai?

A prion is simply a misfolded protein with no genetic material.

question_english: What is the cytoskeleton and what are its functions?
question_hinglish: Cytoskeleton kya hai aur iske functions kya hain?
answer_english: The cytoskeleton is a network of fine fibres in eukaryotic cells. It provides structural support, maintains the shape of the cell, and enables cell movement and internal transport.

It provides structural support to the cell and helps maintain the cell's shape. It also enables the movement of the cell and the transport of materials inside it. The cytoskeleton is visible as a separate entity only under an electron microscope.

subject: Biology
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life
question_english: Mature human red blood cells do not have a nucleus. How does this help them, and what is its disadvantage?
question_hinglish: Mature human RBCs mein nucleus nahi hota. Isse unhe kya fayda hai aur kya nuksaan?
answer_english: The absence of a nucleus provides more space for haemoglobin, so RBCs can carry a larger amount of oxygen to all cells of the body. However, since they lack a nucleus, they cannot repair or divide themselves, so their lifespan is short, about 120 days.
answer_hinglish: Nucleus na hone se haemoglobin ke liye zyada jagah milti hai, toh RBCs body ke saare cells tak zyada oxygen le ja paate hain. Lekin nucleus na hone ki wajah se yeh khud ko repair ya divide nahi kar sakte, isliye inki lifespan short hoti hai, lagbhag 120 din.
ncert_context: Some cells are specialised for particular functions. Mature red blood cells in humans are enucleate, meaning they have no nucleus. This leaves more room inside the cell for haemoglobin, allowing RBCs to transport more oxygen to the body's cells. The trade-off is that, without a nucleus, these cells cannot repair or divide themselves, and they survive only about 120 days.

subject: Biology
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life
question_english: Who discovered the Golgi apparatus and why was its existence doubted at first?
question_hinglish: Golgi apparatus kisne discover kiya tha, aur shuru mein iske existence pe shak kyun kiya gaya?
answer_english: The Golgi apparatus was first observed in 1898 by the Italian scientist Camillo Golgi in the nerve cells of a barn owl. Its existence was doubted because early microscopes could not resolve it clearly, but electron microscope observations confirmed it decades later.
answer_hinglish: Golgi apparatus ko 1898 mein Italian scientist Camillo Golgi ne barn owl ke nerve cells mein pehli baar dekha tha. Shuru mein log shak karte the kyunki purane microscopes ise clearly dikha nahi paate the. Baad mein, decades later, electron microscope ne iska existence confirm kiya.
ncert_context: In 1898, Italian scientist Camillo Golgi used special staining techniques to study the nerve cells of a barn owl and observed a thread-like network. Since the microscopes of that time could not show this structure clearly, many scientists doubted it was real. Decades later, electron microscopes revealed it clearly, and the structure was named the Golgi apparatus in his honour.

question_english: What are lysosomes, and how do they keep the cell clean?
question_hinglish: Lysosomes kya hote hain aur yeh cell ko saaf kaise rakhte hain?
answer_english: Lysosomes are single membrane-bound sacs filled with enzymes. These enzymes break down unwanted proteins, carbohydrates, fats and even damaged parts of the cell. The products of breakdown are released into the cytoplasm, where they may be reused.
answer_hinglish: Lysosomes single membrane wale sacs hote hain jo enzymes se bhare hote hain. Yeh enzymes unwanted proteins, carbohydrates, fats aur cell ke damaged parts ko bhi break down kar dete hain. Breakdown se jo products bante hain woh cytoplasm mein release hote hain aur dobara use ho sakte hain.
ncert_context: During their activities, cells produce waste materials and worn-out organelles. To prevent these from accumulating, cells have a clean-up system called lysosomes. Lysosomes are sacs bounded by a single membrane and filled with enzymes. These enzymes digest unwanted proteins, carbohydrates, fats and damaged cell parts. The products formed are released into the cytoplasm and may be used again in other cellular processes.

question_english: How do lysosomal enzymes in human sperm cells help in fertilisation?
question_hinglish: Human sperm cells ke lysosomal enzymes fertilisation mein kaise help karte hain?

answer_hinglish: Human sperm cells mein lysosomal enzymes hote hain. Jab sperm egg se milta hai, toh yeh enzymes egg ki outer layer ko break down karne mein help karte hain, jisse fertilisation ho paata hai.
ncert_context: Lysosomes contain enzymes that can break down various substances. This ability is put to special use in human sperm cells, which carry lysosomal enzymes. During fertilisation, the sperm must get through the outer layer of the egg. When a sperm meets an egg, its lysosomal enzymes help break down this outer layer, making it possible for fertilisation to happen.

question_english: Why are mitochondria called the powerhouses of the cell?
question_hinglish: Mitochondria ko cell ka powerhouse kyun kehte hain?
answer_english: Mitochondria are called the powerhouses of the cell because they supply the energy needed for most cellular activities. In mitochondria, glucose and other molecules are broken down during cellular respiration to release energy, which is stored as ATP.
answer_hinglish: Kyunki mitochondria hi cell ki zyada tar activities ke liye energy dete hain. Inke andar cellular respiration mein glucose aur doosre molecules break down hote hain aur energy release hoti hai, jo ATP ke form mein store hoti hai.
ncert_context: Every cell needs energy to carry out its activities. Mitochondria supply most of this energy. Inside them, glucose and other molecules are broken down in a process called cellular respiration, releasing energy. This energy is stored in the form of a molecule called Adenosine Triphosphate (ATP), which the cell uses for most of its work. For this reason, mitochondria are known as the powerhouses of the cell.

question_english: Compare the outer and inner membranes of a mitochondrion.
question_hinglish: Mitochondrion ki outer aur inner membrane ko compare karo.
answer_english: The outer membrane of a mitochondrion is smooth and porous. The inner membrane is folded into finger-like projections called cristae, which increase the surface area for chemical reactions and facilitate energy production.
answer_hinglish: Mitochondrion ki outer membrane smooth aur porous hoti hai. Inner membrane finger jaise projections mein folded hoti hai jinhe cristae kehte hain. Cristae chemical reactions ke liye surface area badhate hain aur energy production mein help karte hain.
ncert_context: Each mitochondrion is surrounded by two membranes with a space between them called the intermembrane space. The outer membrane is smooth and porous. The inner membrane, however, is not flat; it is folded into finger-like projections called cristae. These folds provide a much larger surface for the chemical reactions that release energy, helping the mitochondrion produce energy efficiently.

question_english: What is ATP and why is it called the energy currency of the cell?
question_hinglish: ATP kya hai aur ise cell ki energy currency kyun kehte hain?
answer_english: ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate) is the molecule in which the energy released during cellular respiration in mitochondria is stored. It is called the energy currency because the cell uses it for most of its activities.
answer_hinglish: ATP yaani Adenosine Triphosphate woh molecule hai jisme mitochondria mein cellular respiration ke dauraan nikli energy store hoti hai. Ise energy currency isliye kehte hain kyunki cell apni zyada tar activities ke liye isi ko use karta hai.
ncert_context: When glucose and other molecules are broken down in the mitochondria during cellular respiration, energy is released. This energy is not used all at once; it is stored in a molecule called Adenosine Triphosphate, or ATP. Whenever the cell needs energy for an activity, it uses ATP. Like money that can be spent on many things, ATP is spent for most cellular activities, so it is called the energy currency.

question_english: What would happen if all the mitochondria were removed from a eukaryotic cell?
question_hinglish: Agar eukaryotic cell se saare mitochondria nikaal diye jaayein toh kya hoga?

subject: Biology

question_english: Describe the structure of a chloroplast.
question_hinglish: Chloroplast ka structure describe karo.
answer_english: A chloroplast is a double-membrane-bound organelle. Inside it is a semi-fluid substance called the stroma, within which there are disc-shaped membrane structures containing chlorophyll. The chloroplast also contains its own DNA and ribosomes.
answer_hinglish: Chloroplast ek double-membrane wala organelle hai. Iske andar stroma naam ka semi-fluid substance hota hai, aur stroma ke andar disc-shaped membrane structures hote hain jinme chlorophyll hota hai. Chloroplast ka apna DNA aur ribosomes bhi hote hain.
ncert_context: Chloroplasts are a type of plastid in which photosynthesis takes place. Like mitochondria, they are bounded by two membranes, an outer and an inner membrane. Inside is a semi-fluid substance called the stroma. Within the stroma lie disc-shaped membrane structures containing the green pigment chlorophyll, which absorbs light energy. Sugars made during photosynthesis are stored in the stroma along with starch granules.

question_english: What features of mitochondria and plastids suggest that they share an evolutionary history with certain bacteria?
question_hinglish: Mitochondria aur plastids ke kaun se features batate hain ki inka evolutionary history kuch bacteria se juda hai?
answer_english: Both mitochondria and plastids have their own DNA and ribosomes, so they can make some of their own proteins. These features are similar to certain bacteria and suggest that mitochondria and plastids share an evolutionary history with these single-celled organisms.
answer_hinglish: Mitochondria aur plastids dono ka apna DNA aur ribosomes hota hai, isliye yeh apne kuch proteins khud bana sakte hain. Yeh features kuch bacteria jaise hain, jisse lagta hai ki inka evolutionary history in single-celled organisms se shared hai.

question_english: Discuss how mitochondria and chloroplasts are structurally and functionally similar and different.
question_hinglish: Mitochondria aur chloroplasts structure aur function mein kaise similar aur kaise different hain?
answer_english: Similarities: both are double-membrane-bound organelles and both have their own DNA and ribosomes. Differences: mitochondria break down glucose during cellular respiration to release energy stored as ATP, while chloroplasts absorb sunlight using chlorophyll to synthesise food by photosynthesis. Mitochondria have an inner membrane folded into cristae, while chloroplasts have stroma with disc-shaped membranes containing chlorophyll.
answer_hinglish: Similarities: dono double-membrane wale organelles hain aur dono ka apna DNA aur ribosomes hota hai. Mitochondria ki inner membrane cristae mein folded hoti hai, aur chloroplast mein stroma ke andar chlorophyll wale disc-shaped membranes hote hain.
ncert_context: Mitochondria and chloroplasts are both double-membrane-bound organelles, and both contain their own DNA and ribosomes. Their jobs, however, are opposite in a sense. Chloroplasts use chlorophyll to absorb sunlight and synthesise sugars during photosynthesis. Mitochondria break down glucose and other molecules during cellular respiration to release energy as ATP. Internally, mitochondria have folded cristae, while chloroplasts have stroma with chlorophyll-containing discs.

question_english: What are chromoplasts and what is their importance?
question_hinglish: Chromoplasts kya hote hain aur inka kya importance hai?
answer_english: Chromoplasts are plastids that contain pigments other than chlorophyll, which may be yellow, orange or red. They give bright colours to flowers and fruits, which help attract pollinators for pollination and fruit-eating animals that help in seed dispersal.
answer_hinglish: Chromoplasts woh plastids hain jinme chlorophyll ke alawa doosre pigments hote hain, jaise yellow, orange ya red. Yeh flowers aur fruits ko bright colours dete hain, jisse pollinators attract hote hain pollination ke liye, aur fruit khaane wale animals bhi aate hain jo seed dispersal mein help karte hain.
ncert_context: Not all plastids are green. In flower petals and fruits, plastids contain pigments other than chlorophyll. These are called chromoplasts, from the Greek word chroma, meaning colour. Their pigments may be yellow, orange or red and are responsible for the bright colours of many flowers and fruits. These colours attract pollinators and fruit-eating animals, helping in pollination and seed dispersal.

question_english: Renu says that all parts of a plant, even roots, contain plastids. Rohit says roots lack plastids because they do not perform photosynthesis. Who is correct? Justify.

subject: Biology
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life
question_english: Describe the structure and functions of the vacuole in a mature plant cell.
question_hinglish: Mature plant cell mein vacuole ka structure aur functions describe karo.
answer_english: A mature plant cell usually has one large central vacuole surrounded by a single selectively permeable membrane and filled with a watery fluid called cell sap. It stores water, minerals, sugars and waste materials, and by storing large amounts of water it maintains pressure inside the cell, keeping the plant cell firm.
answer_hinglish: Mature plant cell mein usually ek bada central vacuole hota hai, jo single selectively permeable membrane se ghira hota hai aur cell sap naam ke watery fluid se bhara hota hai. Yeh paani, minerals, sugars aur waste store karta hai, aur bahut saara paani store karke cell ke andar pressure maintain karta hai, jisse plant cell firm rehta hai.
ncert_context: Vacuoles are the organelles for storage and support. In a mature plant cell, there is usually one large central vacuole enclosed by a single selectively permeable membrane. It is filled with a watery fluid called cell sap and stores water, minerals, sugars and waste materials. Because it holds a lot of water, the vacuole maintains pressure within the cell, which keeps the plant cell firm.

question_english: Why do plants look wilted when they do not get enough water?
question_hinglish: Jab plants ko kaafi paani nahi milta toh woh murjhaye hue kyun dikhte hain?
answer_english: When a plant does not get enough water, the vacuoles in its cells lose water. As a result, the pressure inside the cells drops, the cells become less firm, and the plant looks wilted.
answer_hinglish: Jab plant ko kaafi paani nahi milta, toh uske cells ke vacuoles paani kho dete hain. Isse cells ke andar ka pressure kam ho jaata hai, cells kam firm ho jaate hain, aur plant murjhaya hua dikhta hai.

question_english: Which of the following pairs of cell organelles contains DNA? (i) Chloroplasts, Ribosomes (ii) Mitochondria, Nucleus (iii) Golgi bodies, Ribosomes (iv) Nucleus, Lysosomes

Other organelles, such as ribosomes, the Golgi apparatus and lysosomes, perform their functions without containing DNA of their own.

question_english: Which structures are present in plant cells but absent in animal cells?

question_english: Describe the experiment by J. Craig Venter and his team in 2010 in synthetic biology.
question_hinglish: 2010 mein J. Craig Venter aur unki team ne synthetic biology mein jo experiment kiya, use describe karo.
answer_english: Venter's team studied the complete DNA sequence of the bacterium Mycoplasma mycoides using computer programming and chemically synthesised an exact copy of it in the laboratory. They removed the DNA from a closely related bacterium, kept the rest of its cell intact, and inserted the synthetic DNA. The cell then grew and divided following the instructions of the synthetic DNA.
answer_hinglish: Venter ki team ne computer programming se bacterium Mycoplasma mycoides ka poora DNA sequence study kiya aur lab mein chemically uski exact copy banayi. ncert_context: In 2010, J. Craig Venter and his team made an important discovery in synthetic biology. They studied the complete DNA sequence of a simple bacterium, Mycoplasma mycoides, and chemically synthesised an exact copy of this DNA. question_english: List the main steps for preparing a slide of onion root tip cells to observe cell division.
question_hinglish: Cell division dekhne ke liye onion root tip cells ki slide banane ke main steps batao.
answer_english:
1. Grow onion roots in a jar of water for 5-6 days.
2. Cut 2-3 cm of fresh roots and keep them in aceto-alcohol for 24 hours, then transfer to 70 per cent ethanol.
3. Wash a root and treat it with dilute HCl for 10-15 minutes to soften the tissue, then rinse.
4. Add 2-3 drops of aceto-carmine stain, leave for 5-10 minutes and warm gently.
5. Cut the tip, place a coverslip, squash gently and observe under a microscope.

question_english: What are the two major types of cell division and the importance of each?
question_hinglish: Cell division ke do major types kaun se hain aur dono ka importance kya hai?

ncert_context: Cell division occurs in two major ways: mitosis and meiosis. It produces gametes and creates genetic diversity among organisms, which is why offspring are similar to but not exactly the same as their parents.

question_english: Explain mitosis and its result.
question_hinglish: Mitosis explain karo aur batao iska result kya hota hai.
answer_english: Mitosis is the most common type of cell division, in which one parent cell produces two genetically identical daughter cells. Each daughter cell gets the same DNA and the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell, so genetic information is largely maintained across body cells.
answer_hinglish: Mitosis cell division ka sabse common type hai, jisme ek parent cell se do genetically identical daughter cells bante hain. Har daughter cell ko parent cell jaisa hi DNA aur utne hi chromosomes milte hain, isliye body cells mein genetic information largely same rehti hai.

Each new cell receives the same DNA and the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell.

question_english: Why is it important that gametes have half the number of chromosomes of the parent cell?

question_english: What are the consequences of errors in mitosis and meiosis?
question_hinglish: Mitosis aur meiosis mein errors hone ke kya consequences hote hain?
answer_english: Errors in mitosis lead to uncontrolled cell divisions, which can cause tumours and an abnormal number of chromosomes in body cells. Errors in meiosis may result in genetic disorders associated with developmental problems or distinctive physical features, and faulty meiosis may also cause early pregnancy loss or reduced fertility.
answer_hinglish: Mitosis mein error se uncontrolled cell division hota hai, jisse tumours aur body cells mein chromosomes ki abnormal number ho sakti hai. question_english: How was the Cell Theory formulated? Name the scientists and their contributions.

answer_english: In 1838, Matthias Schleiden, a German botanist, reported that all plants are made up of cells. question_english: What is totipotency? Who proposed this idea?
question_hinglish: Totipotency kya hai? Yeh idea kisne diya tha?
answer_english: Totipotency is the special ability of plant cells to develop into a complete plant and form different types of cells when provided with suitable nutrients and favourable conditions. It was proposed in 1902 by the Austrian botanist Gottlieb Haberlandt.
answer_hinglish: Totipotency plant cells ki woh special ability hai jisse woh suitable nutrients aur favourable conditions milne pe ek complete plant mein develop ho sakte hain aur alag-alag types ke cells bana sakte hain. Yeh idea 1902 mein Austrian botanist Gottlieb Haberlandt ne diya tha.
ncert_context: In 1902, Austrian botanist Gottlieb Haberlandt proposed that any living plant cell, even a fully mature cell from a permanent tissue, can develop into a complete plant if given suitable nutrients and favourable conditions. He suggested that plant cells can form different types of cells and also change them. This special ability is called totipotency, and his idea laid the foundation for Plant Tissue Culture Technology.

question_english: A carrot placed in plain water stays stiff and crunchy, while a carrot placed in concentrated salt solution becomes rubbery and limp. Explain why.
question_hinglish: Plain water mein rakhi gajar stiff aur crunchy rehti hai, jabki concentrated salt solution mein rakhi gajar rubbery aur dheeli ho jaati hai. Kyun?
answer_english: In plain water, water enters the carrot cells by osmosis, keeping them full and firm, so the carrot stays stiff and crunchy. In concentrated salt solution, water moves out of the carrot cells by osmosis into the more concentrated solution, so the cells lose water and become less firm, making the carrot rubbery and limp.
answer_hinglish: Plain water mein osmosis se paani gajar ke cells ke andar jaata hai, cells bhare aur firm rehte hain, isliye gajar stiff aur crunchy rehti hai. Concentrated salt solution mein osmosis se paani cells se bahar nikal jaata hai, cells paani kho ke kam firm ho jaate hain, isliye gajar rubbery aur dheeli ho jaati hai.
ncert_context: Osmosis is the movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane from a dilute solution to a concentrated one. Plain water has less solute than cell contents, so water enters cells. A concentrated salt solution has more solute, so water leaves cells. In plant cells, water stored in vacuoles maintains pressure that keeps cells firm; when cells lose water, they become less firm.

question_english: How do high concentrations of salt and sugar prevent the growth of spoilage-causing bacteria and fungi in pickles?
question_hinglish: Pickles mein salt aur sugar ki high concentration spoilage karne wale bacteria aur fungi ko grow hone se kaise rokti hai?

Bacteria and fungi are made of cells surrounded by a cell membrane and cell wall, through which water can pass. Like a potato piece in salt solution that shrinks as it loses water, these microorganisms lose water in a highly concentrated medium.

subject: Biology
question_english: What is a tissue?

In unicellular organisms such as amoeba, by contrast, a single cell performs all the functions of life.

question_english: How does the formation of different tissues lead to division of labour? Give examples.
question_hinglish: Alag-alag tissues banne se division of labour kaise hota hai? Examples do.
answer_english: When different groups of cells form different tissues, each tissue performs a specific function. For example, in animals, muscle tissue enables movement and nervous tissue carries messages; in plants, xylem transports water and minerals while phloem transports food.

question_english: Why are plant tissues different from animal tissues?
question_hinglish: Plant tissues animal tissues se alag kyun hote hain?
answer_english: Most plants are fixed in one place and need support to stay firm and upright, so plant cells have a rigid cell wall. Animals move, and without a cell wall their cells change shape easily, making their bodies suitable for locomotion. Plants and animals also differ in their mode of nutrition, in tissues for transporting food and water, and in growth patterns, so their tissues differ in structure and function.
answer_hinglish: Zyada tar plants ek jagah fixed rehte hain aur unhe firm aur seedha rehne ke liye support chahiye, isliye plant cells mein rigid cell wall hoti hai. Animals move karte hain, aur cell wall na hone se unke cells aasani se shape badal lete hain, jo locomotion ke liye suitable hai. Plants aur animals ka mode of nutrition, food aur paani transport karne wale tissues aur growth patterns bhi alag hote hain, isliye unke tissues bhi alag hote hain.

question_hinglish: Meristematic tissue ke cells ki characteristics batao.
answer_english: Cells of meristematic tissue are small, have thin cell walls, a large and prominent nucleus, and dense cytoplasm with many organelles. Vacuoles are generally absent, and the cells are tightly packed with little or no intercellular space.
answer_hinglish: Meristematic tissue ke cells chhote hote hain, unki cell walls patli hoti hain, nucleus bada aur prominent hota hai, aur cytoplasm dense hota hai jisme kai organelles hote hain. Vacuoles generally nahi hote, aur cells tightly packed hote hain jinke beech bahut kam ya bilkul intercellular space nahi hota.
ncert_context: The cells of meristematic tissues are small and have thin cell walls. They have a large and prominent nucleus and dense cytoplasm containing many organelles. Vacuoles are generally absent, and the cells are tightly packed with little or no intercellular space. These characteristics of meristematic tissue allow continuous and rapid cell division, which adds new cells to the plant body.

subject: Biology
question_english: Why do you think the cells of meristematic tissues lack vacuoles?
question_hinglish: Meristematic tissues ke cells mein vacuoles kyun nahi hote?
answer_english: Meristematic cells are specialised for continuous and rapid cell division, so they are filled with dense cytoplasm, many organelles and a large nucleus. Vacuoles are storage organelles, and since these cells are not meant for storage, vacuoles are generally absent.
answer_hinglish: Meristematic cells lagataar aur fast divide hone ke liye specialised hote hain, isliye inme dense cytoplasm, kai organelles aur bada nucleus hota hai. Vacuoles storage organelles hain, aur kyunki in cells ka kaam storage nahi hai, isliye inme vacuoles generally nahi hote.
ncert_context: Meristematic cells are small, thin-walled and tightly packed, with a large prominent nucleus and dense cytoplasm with many organelles. Vacuoles are generally absent. These characteristics allow continuous and rapid cell division. In mature plant cells, by contrast, a large central vacuole stores water, minerals, sugars and waste. Permanent tissues, not meristematic tissues, become specialised for functions such as storage.

subject: Biology
question_english: Vibha claims that meristematic cells are located only at the root and shoot apices. Is she correct?
question_hinglish: Vibha kehti hai ki meristematic cells sirf root aur shoot apices pe hi hote hain. Kya woh sahi hai?
answer_english: Vibha is not correct. Apical meristems are present at the root and shoot tips, but lateral meristem is present along the circumference of stems and increases girth, and intercalary meristem is present at the base of the internode or just above the node.
answer_hinglish: Vibha sahi nahi hai. Apical meristems root aur shoot tips pe hote hain, lekin lateral meristem stems ki circumference ke along hota hai aur girth badhata hai, aur intercalary meristem internode ke base pe ya node ke theek upar hota hai.
ncert_context: Plants have three types of meristematic tissues. The apical meristem is located at the root and shoot tips and increases length. The lateral meristem, made of actively dividing cells arranged in a ring in the stem, is located along the circumference of stems and increases girth. The intercalary meristem is located at the base of the internode or just above the node and helps plants regenerate after cutting.

subject: Biology
question_english: What is differentiation in plant tissues?
question_hinglish: Plant tissues mein differentiation kya hota hai?
answer_english: Differentiation is the process by which meristematic tissue becomes specialised to perform specific functions. Cells that lose the ability to divide undergo changes in structure and function and become permanent tissues.
answer_hinglish: Differentiation woh process hai jisme meristematic tissue specific functions karne ke liye specialised ho jaata hai. Jo cells divide karne ki ability kho dete hain, unke structure aur function mein changes aate hain aur woh permanent tissues ban jaate hain.
ncert_context: Due to continuous cell division, meristematic tissue adds new cells to the plant body. Some of the newly formed cells remain meristematic, while others lose the ability to divide. The cells that lose this ability undergo changes in structure and function and become permanent tissues specialised for functions such as support, transport or storage. This process is called differentiation.

subject: Biology
question_english: Differentiate between simple and complex permanent tissues with examples.
question_hinglish: Simple aur complex permanent tissues mein difference batao, examples ke saath.
answer_english: Simple permanent tissues are composed of only one type of cell, for example parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma. Complex permanent tissues are composed of more than one type of cell working together, for example xylem and phloem.
answer_hinglish: Simple permanent tissues sirf ek type ke cells se bane hote hain, jaise parenchyma, collenchyma aur sclerenchyma. Complex permanent tissues ek se zyada type ke cells se bane hote hain jo milkar kaam karte hain, jaise xylem aur phloem.
ncert_context: Permanent tissues are formed when meristematic cells lose the ability to divide and become specialised. Permanent tissues can be simple or complex. Simple permanent tissues are composed of only one type of cell; these include parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma. Complex permanent tissues are composed of more than one type of cell working together; xylem and phloem are complex permanent tissues that transport water and food.

subject: Biology
question_english: Differentiate between meristematic and permanent tissues.
question_hinglish: Meristematic aur permanent tissues mein difference batao.
answer_english: Meristematic tissues consist of actively dividing cells that are small, thin-walled, tightly packed and generally lack vacuoles; they are responsible for growth. Permanent tissues consist of cells that have lost the ability to divide and have become specialised through differentiation to perform functions such as support, transport or storage.
answer_hinglish: Meristematic tissues mein actively divide hone wale cells hote hain jo chhote, patli wall wale, tightly packed hote hain aur generally inme vacuoles nahi hote; yeh growth ke liye responsible hain. Permanent tissues ke cells divide karne ki ability kho chuke hote hain aur differentiation se support, transport ya storage jaise kaam ke liye specialised ho jaate hain.
ncert_context: Plant tissues are broadly classified into meristematic and permanent tissues, depending on their ability to divide. Meristematic tissue cells divide continuously and rapidly; they are small, thin-walled, tightly packed and usually lack vacuoles. Some new cells lose the ability to divide and, through differentiation, become permanent tissues specialised to perform specific functions, such as support, transport or storage.

subject: Biology
question_english: Describe the structure and functions of the epidermis in plants.
question_hinglish: Plants mein epidermis ka structure aur functions describe karo.
answer_english: The epidermis is the outermost layer of the plant body, made of a tightly packed single layer of flat, rectangular cells. It protects all parts of the plant from mechanical injury, water loss, harmful microorganisms and extreme environmental conditions. Its cells are covered with a waxy layer of cutin called the cuticle.
answer_hinglish: Epidermis plant body ki sabse bahar wali layer hai, jo flat aur rectangular cells ki ek tightly packed single layer se bani hoti hai. Yeh plant ke saare parts ko mechanical injury, water loss, harmful microorganisms aur extreme environmental conditions se protect karti hai. Iske cells ke upar cutin ki ek waxy layer hoti hai jise cuticle kehte hain.
ncert_context: The epidermis forms the outermost layer of the plant body. It consists of a tightly packed, single layer of flat and rectangular cells and protects all parts of the plant from mechanical injury, water loss, harmful microorganisms and extreme environmental conditions. These cells are covered with a waxy layer of cutin called the cuticle. In roots, epidermal projections form root hair, and in leaves, the epidermis contains stomata.

subject: Biology
question_english: What is the cuticle and what are its functions?
question_hinglish: Cuticle kya hai aur iske functions kya hain?
answer_english: The cuticle is a waxy layer of cutin covering the epidermal cells. It reduces water loss during transpiration and provides protection against mechanical injury and invasion by parasites. Plants in very dry habitats may have a thick cuticle.
answer_hinglish: Cuticle cutin ki ek waxy layer hai jo epidermal cells ko cover karti hai. Yeh transpiration ke dauraan water loss kam karti hai aur mechanical injury aur parasites ke attack se protection deti hai. Bahut dry jagahon ke plants mein cuticle thick hoti hai.
ncert_context: The epidermal cells of plants are covered with a waxy layer of cutin called the cuticle. In some plants living in very dry habitats, the epidermis may be covered by a thick layer of cuticle to reduce water loss in the process of transpiration through stomata. The cuticle also provides protection against mechanical injury and invasion by parasites.

question_english: Why does a fresh twig bend but a dry twig break?

question_english: Name the three tissue systems in plants and state what each consists of.
question_hinglish: Plants ke teen tissue systems ke naam batao aur har ek mein kya hota hai.
answer_english:
1. Dermal tissue system: forms the outer covering of the plant, protects inner parts and reduces water loss.
2. Ground tissue system: forms the main body of the plant between dermal and conducting tissues and includes parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma.
3. Vascular tissue system: consists of the conducting tissues, xylem and phloem.

question_english: A textbook states that each plant tissue performs only one specific function. Give examples to examine this statement.

answer_english: The statement is not fully correct. Parenchyma mainly stores food, but it also performs photosynthesis in green parts and forms air spaces in aquatic plants. subject: Biology
question_english: How is the bark of a tree formed?
question_hinglish: Tree ki bark kaise banti hai?
answer_english: As plants grow older, some cells below the epidermis of the stem develop the ability to divide, act as lateral meristematic cells and form the cork cambium. Division of cork cambium cells gives rise to cork cells, which are dead, compactly arranged and impermeable to water and gases. These form the bark of the tree.
answer_hinglish: Jaise-jaise plants budhe hote hain, stem ki epidermis ke neeche ke kuch cells divide karne ki ability develop kar lete hain, lateral meristematic cells ki tarah kaam karte hain aur cork cambium banate hain. Cork cambium ke division se cork cells bante hain, jo dead, compactly arranged aur paani aur gases ke liye impermeable hote hain. Yahi tree ki bark banate hain.

As plants grow older, some cells below the epidermis of the stem develop the ability to divide, act as lateral meristematic cells and form the cork cambium. Division of cork cambium cells gives rise to cork cells. Cork cells are dead, compactly arranged, and contain a substance which makes them impermeable to water and gases. This forms the bark.

subject: Biology
question_english: An elephant severely debarked a tree for food. Which function of the tree is hampered by debarking, and what would happen if the tissues beneath the bark were also damaged?
question_hinglish: Ek elephant ne khane ke liye ek tree ki bark buri tarah utaar di. Debarking se tree ka kaun sa function affect hota hai, aur agar bark ke neeche ke tissues bhi damage ho jaayein toh kya hoga?
answer_english: Bark is made of cork cells that are impermeable to water and gases and protect the stem, so debarking hampers protection of the inner tissues. There are three types of muscles. Skeletal muscles are attached to the skeleton and carry out voluntary movements; their fibres are long, cylindrical, unbranched, multinucleate and striated. Smooth muscles are in organs like the stomach and intestines; their cells are spindle-shaped, uninucleate and unstriated. Cardiac muscles are found only in the heart; their fibres are cylindrical, branched, uninucleate with faint striations and work rhythmically.

Question:
Compare skeletal, smooth and cardiac muscles.

Intent Type: compare_concepts
Answer the question in English using only the given context.

Skeletal muscle: attached to the skeleton, voluntary; fibres long, cylindrical, unbranched, multinucleate and striated. Smooth muscle: in stomach and intestines, involuntary; cells spindle-shaped, single nucleus, no striations. Cardiac muscle: only in the heart, involuntary; fibres cylindrical, branched, single nucleus, faint striations, work without fatigue.

subject: Biology
question_english: Assertion (A): Cardiac muscle can contract continuously without fatigue. Reason (R): Cardiac muscle cells have a high number of mitochondria and an abundant blood supply. Choose: (i) Both A and R true, R explains A (ii) Both true, R does not explain A (iii) A true, R false (iv) A false, R true

subject: Biology
question_english: What is the role of nervous tissue in the body?
question_hinglish: Body mein nervous tissue ka kya role hai?
answer_english: Nervous tissue forms the body's control and coordination network. It controls actions like pulling the hand away from something hot or remembering things, with the brain acting as the control centre. Muscles cannot function independently; they receive instructions from the nervous tissue.
answer_hinglish: Nervous tissue body ka control aur coordination network banata hai. Garam cheez se haath hatana ya cheezein yaad rakhna jaise actions yahi control karta hai, aur brain control centre ki tarah kaam karta hai. Muscles khud se kaam nahi kar sakte; unhe instructions nervous tissue se milte hain.

Muscles, both voluntary and involuntary, cannot function independently; they receive instructions from nervous tissue.

subject: Biology
question_english: Describe the structure of a neuron and the function of each part.
question_hinglish: Neuron ka structure describe karo aur har part ka function batao.
answer_english: A neuron has three main parts: the cell body, which contains the nucleus and controls cell activities; dendrites, which receive signals from other neurons; and an axon, a long fibre that carries messages from the cell and ends at axon terminals, which transmit messages to other cells.
answer_hinglish: Neuron ke teen main parts hote hain: cell body, jisme nucleus hota hai aur jo cell ki activities control karti hai; dendrites, jo doosre neurons se signals receive karte hain; aur axon, ek lamba fibre jo cell se messages le jaata hai aur axon terminals pe khatam hota hai, jo messages doosre cells tak transmit karte hain.
ncert_context: The cells of nervous tissue are called neurons or nerve cells, and they are specialised to receive, process and transmit messages. Each neuron has three main parts. The cell body contains the nucleus and controls cell activities. Dendrites receive signals from other neurons. The axon is a long fibre that carries messages away from the cell and ends at axon terminals, which transmit the messages to other cells.

subject: Biology
question_english: How do muscles produce movement at a joint?
question_hinglish: Muscles joint pe movement kaise produce karte hain?
answer_english: Muscles are attached to bones by strong, flexible bands called tendons. When a muscle contracts, the tendon transmits this force to the bone, resulting in movement at a joint. Joints allow movement, but they cannot move bones on their own.
answer_hinglish: Muscles bones se tendons naam ke strong, flexible bands se jude hote hain. Jab muscle contract hota hai, toh tendon yeh force bone tak transmit karta hai, aur joint pe movement hota hai. Joints movement allow karte hain, lekin khud se bones ko move nahi kar sakte.
ncert_context: Muscles pull on bones to produce movement. They are attached to bones by strong, flexible bands called tendons. When a muscle contracts, the tendon transmits this force to the bone, resulting in movement at a joint. A joint is a junction between two or more bones. Joints allow movement, but they cannot move the bones on their own; the pull of the muscles is needed.

subject: Biology
question_english: What percentage of the body weight of an adult is made up by the skeleton and by muscles?
question_hinglish: Adult ki body weight ka kitna percentage skeleton aur kitna muscles se aata hai?

subject: Biology
question_english: An adult male weighs 60 kg. Using an average bone mass of 15 per cent and muscle mass of 45 per cent, estimate the weight of his bones and muscles.
question_hinglish: Ek adult male ka weight 60 kg hai. Average bone mass 15 per cent aur muscle mass 45 per cent maan ke uske bones aur muscles ka weight estimate karo.
answer_english:
Given: body weight = 60 kg, bone = 15%, muscle = 45%.
Step 1: Bone weight = 60 x 15/100 = 9 kg.
Step 2: Muscle weight = 60 x 45/100 = 27 kg.
His bones weigh about 9 kg and his muscles about 27 kg.

question_english: Describe F. C. Steward's experiment on carrot phloem cells.
question_hinglish: F. C. Steward ke carrot phloem cells wale experiment ko describe karo.

Woh pehle insaan the jinhone dikhaya ki single cells mein bhi poora plant banane ki ability hoti hai.

subject: Biology
question_english: What do the terms dedifferentiation and redifferentiation mean in Steward's experiment?
question_hinglish: Steward ke experiment mein dedifferentiation aur redifferentiation ka kya matlab hai?
answer_english: Dedifferentiation is the process in which mature phloem cells regain the ability to divide and form an undifferentiated mass of unspecialised cells. Redifferentiation is when these cells, grown in appropriate conditions with nutrients and growth chemicals, divide further and form roots, shoot and eventually a complete plant.
answer_hinglish: Dedifferentiation mein mature phloem cells phir se divide karne ki ability paa lete hain aur unspecialised cells ka ek undifferentiated mass bana dete hain. ncert_context: Steward's experiment showed that carrot phloem cells first dedifferentiated, meaning the cells regained the ability to divide, forming an undifferentiated mass of unspecialised cells. When grown in appropriate conditions supplemented with nutrients and growth chemicals, these cells further divided and redifferentiated to form roots, shoot and eventually the complete plant. Thus, some mature plant cells can undifferentiate, divide and redifferentiate.

subject: Biology
question_english: What is crown gall disease and what causes it?
question_hinglish: Crown gall disease kya hai aur yeh kis wajah se hoti hai?

answer_hinglish: Crown gall disease ek plant disease hai jisme fast aur uncontrolled cell division ki wajah se stems pe tumour jaisi swellings ban jaati hain. Yeh Agrobacterium tumefaciens naam ke bacterium se hoti hai.

Scientists studied how this bacterium transfers its genetic material into plant cells, and this knowledge was later used in plant tissue culture and genetic engineering.

subject: Biology
question_english: Sohan grew sugarcane from two types of cuttings, A and B. Type B sprouted into plants but type A did not. Why could type B grow?
question_hinglish: Sohan ne do type ki cuttings, A aur B, se sugarcane ugaya. Type B se plants ug aaye lekin type A se nahi. Type B kyun ug paaya?
answer_english: Type B cuttings likely included a node, where the intercalary meristem is located at the base of the internode or just above the node. This meristematic tissue allows the cutting to regenerate and sprout. Type A cuttings lacked a node and therefore lacked this meristem, so they could not sprout.
answer_hinglish: Type B cuttings mein shayad node tha, jahan internode ke base pe ya node ke upar intercalary meristem hota hai. Yahi meristematic tissue cutting ko regenerate aur sprout karne deta hai. Type A cuttings mein node nahi tha, isliye yeh meristem bhi nahi tha, aur woh ug nahi paayi.
ncert_context: The node is the point on a stem where branches or leaves arise, and the part between two nodes is the internode. The intercalary meristem is located at the base of the internode or just above the node, and it helps plants such as grasses regenerate after being cut. When the tip of a young stem is cut, new branches arise from the nodes of the stem.

subject: Biology
question_english: A teak tree has a diameter of 8 cm at 10 years and 40 cm at 40 years, with 10 and 40 annual rings respectively. What is the average increase in diameter per year between 10 and 40 years, and what is the relation between age and number of rings?
question_hinglish: Ek teak tree ka diameter 10 saal pe 8 cm aur 40 saal pe 40 cm hai, aur annual rings kramashah 10 aur 40 hain. 10 se 40 saal ke beech diameter har saal average kitna badha, aur age aur rings ki number mein kya relation hai?
answer_english:
Given: diameter at 10 years = 8 cm, at 40 years = 40 cm.
Step 1: Increase in diameter = 40 - 8 = 32 cm.
Step 2: Time = 40 - 10 = 30 years.
Step 3: Average increase = 32 / 30 = about 1.07 cm per year.
The number of annual rings equals the age of the tree, since one ring forms each year; the diameter increases due to the lateral meristem.

subject: Biology
question_english: A plant cell and an animal cell are of the same size. Which will have a larger vacuole and why?
question_hinglish: Ek plant cell aur ek animal cell same size ke hain. Kiska vacuole bada hoga aur kyun?
answer_english: The plant cell will have a larger vacuole. A mature plant cell usually has one large central vacuole that stores water, minerals and sugars and keeps the cell firm, while vacuoles in animal cells are only sometimes present and are much smaller. This assumes the plant cell is mature and not a meristematic cell, which generally lacks vacuoles.
answer_hinglish: Plant cell ka vacuole bada hoga. Yahan assumption hai ki plant cell mature hai, meristematic nahi, kyunki meristematic cells mein generally vacuoles nahi hote.

subject: Biology
question_english: What is reproduction and why is it important?
question_hinglish: Reproduction kya hai aur yeh important kyun hai?

answer_hinglish: Reproduction ek biological process hai jisse living beings apni hi kind ke naye individuals paida karte hain. Yeh important hai kyunki har organism ki ek definite life span hoti hai, aur reproduction se hi Earth pe life continue rehti hai.

For example, a mango tree may die, but its seeds grow as new mango plants.

subject: Biology
question_english: Differentiate between asexual and sexual reproduction.
question_hinglish: Asexual aur sexual reproduction mein difference batao.

In sexual reproduction, offspring inherit a mix of characteristics from two individuals. This mixing may lead to small differences between parents and their young ones. Accumulated over many generations, such differences help living beings adapt to changing environments, and sometimes even give rise to new species.

subject: Biology
question_english: Why does vegetative propagation produce genetically identical individuals?
question_hinglish: Vegetative propagation se genetically identical individuals kyun bante hain?
answer_english: Vegetative propagation involves only one parent, so the offspring are genetically identical to it. The central process behind asexual reproduction is mitosis, which produces daughter cells with the same chromosomes as the parent cell.
answer_hinglish: Vegetative propagation mein sirf ek parent hota hai, isliye offspring genetically us jaise hi hote hain. Asexual reproduction ke peeche main process mitosis hai, jo parent cell jaise hi chromosomes wale daughter cells banata hai.

Because of this, the offspring are genetically identical to the parent and are called clones.

question_english: Describe the method of propagating plants by cutting.

subject: Biology
question_english: Explain the process of grafting with an example.
question_hinglish: Grafting ka process example ke saath explain karo.
answer_english: In grafting, a healthy rooted plant (Plant A), such as a wild rose, is taken and a slit is made on its twig. A healthy stem piece from another variety (Plant B), such as a yellow or pink rose, is inserted and fitted into the slit. The joint is protected with cotton cloth or wrapping film until it heals, the other branches of Plant A are cut, and the plant is watered regularly.

Doosri variety (Plant B), jaise yellow ya pink rose, ka healthy stem piece is slit mein fit kiya jaata hai. Joint ko heal hone tak cotton cloth ya wrapping film se protect kiya jaata hai, Plant A ki baaki branches kaat di jaati hain, aur regularly paani diya jaata hai.

subject: Biology
question_english: Describe how a new plant is produced by layering.
question_hinglish: Layering se naya plant kaise banta hai, describe karo.
answer_english: In layering, a flexible, thin twig of a tree or shrub, such as lemon, is bent and its middle part is buried under the soil and watered regularly. After 10 to 15 days, roots develop from the buried part. Once roots have formed, the twig is cut from the parent plant so it can grow as a new plant.
answer_hinglish: Layering mein lemon jaise tree ya shrub ki ek flexible, patli twig ka beech ka hissa soil mein daba diya jaata hai aur regularly paani diya jaata hai. 10 se 15 din mein dabe hue hisse se roots nikal aati hain. Roots banne ke baad twig ko parent plant se kaat diya jaata hai taaki woh naye plant ki tarah grow kare.

question_english: How has tissue culture revolutionised banana farming?
question_hinglish: Tissue culture ne banana farming ko kaise badal diya hai?

question_english: Describe spores and explain how they help fungi spread.
question_hinglish: Spores describe karo aur batao yeh fungi ko phailne mein kaise help karte hain.

They float easily through air currents and germinate quickly into new individuals when they find moisture and nutrients.
