subject: Biology
question_english: Why is the moist chamber for growing bread mould kept warm, and why do we refrigerate perishable food?
question_hinglish: Bread mould ugane wala moist chamber garam kyun rakha jaata hai, aur hum perishable food ko fridge mein kyun rakhte hain?
answer_english: The moist chamber is kept warm (25 to 35 °C) because mould spores need warmth and moisture to grow. Lower temperatures slow or stop their reproduction, which is why refrigerating perishable food prevents spoilage from moulds and bacteria.
answer_hinglish: Moist chamber ko garam (25 se 35 °C) isliye rakhte hain kyunki mould spores ko ugne ke liye warmth aur moisture chahiye. Kam temperature pe unka reproduction slow ya band ho jaata hai, isliye perishable food ko fridge mein rakhne se woh moulds aur bacteria se kharab nahi hota.
ncert_context: The moist chamber is kept warm at 25 to 35 °C because spores of mould present in the air need warmth and moisture to grow on bread or roti. Lower temperatures slow or stop their reproduction, which is why we refrigerate perishable food. Before refrigerators became common about 100 years ago, fresh food lasted only 1 to 2 days. Refrigeration revolutionised food habits and prevents spoilage from moulds and bacteria.

subject: Biology
question_english: Why are offspring produced by asexual reproduction called clones?
question_hinglish: Asexual reproduction se bane offspring ko clones kyun kehte hain?
answer_english: The central process behind asexual reproduction is mitosis, which produces daughter cells with the same number of chromosomes identical to the parent cell. So the offspring are genetically identical to the parent, and such genetically identical offspring are called clones.
answer_hinglish: Asexual reproduction ke peeche main process mitosis hai, jo parent cell jaise hi identical chromosomes wale daughter cells banata hai. Isliye offspring genetically parent jaise hi hote hain, aur aise genetically identical offspring ko clones kehte hain.
ncert_context: In all the organisms studied that reproduce asexually, the central process is mitosis, a type of cell division that produces two daughter cells, each having the same number of chromosomes identical to the parent cell. Because of this, the offspring produced are genetically identical to the parent and are called clones. This method is fast and helps organisms increase their population quickly, especially when conditions are favourable.

question_english: Why does asexual reproduction produce offspring that are genetically identical to the parent?
question_hinglish: Asexual reproduction se bane offspring parent jaise genetically identical kyun hote hain?

question_english: Differentiate between self-pollination and cross-pollination.

question_english: Describe the process of fertilisation in flowering plants.
question_hinglish: Flowering plants mein fertilisation ka process describe karo.
answer_english: Once pollen reaches a compatible stigma, it produces a pollen tube that grows down through the style into the ovary. The male gamete moves through this tube to the ovule, where it fuses with the egg cell. This fusion is called fertilisation, and the fertilised egg, called the zygote, later develops into an embryo.

Male gamete is tube se hote hue ovule tak pahunchta hai aur egg cell se fuse ho jaata hai. Is fusion ko fertilisation kehte hain, aur fertilised egg, jise zygote kehte hain, aage chalkar embryo ban jaata hai.

subject: Biology
question_english: Who was P. Maheshwari and what were his contributions?
question_hinglish: P. Maheshwari kaun the aur unke contributions kya the?
answer_english: P. Maheshwari, known as the 'Father of Indian Embryology', was a leading scientist in the study of plant reproductive organs. He developed in-vitro fertilisation in flowering plants by fusing an egg and male gamete in a test tube to create hybrid plants, was one of the first to grow plant embryos on artificial nutrient media, and wrote the classic book An Introduction to the Embryology of Angiosperms (1950).
answer_hinglish: P. Maheshwari, jinhe 'Father of Indian Embryology' kaha jaata hai, plant reproductive organs ki study ke leading scientist the. question_hinglish: External aur internal fertilisation mein difference batao, examples ke saath.

subject: Biology
question_english: Explain the larval strategy used by fish, amphibians and insects to nourish their young.
question_hinglish: Fish, amphibians aur insects apne young ko nourish karne ke liye jo larval strategy use karte hain, use explain karo.
answer_english: These animals produce hundreds to thousands of eggs at a time, and the mother cannot provide large quantities of yolk for so many eggs. answer_hinglish: Yeh animals ek baar mein hundreds se thousands eggs dete hain, aur mother itne saare eggs ke liye bahut saara yolk nahi de sakti. Larva organic wastes kha kar grow karta hai; is feeding stage ke baad transformation hota hai aur adult body banti hai, jaise butterflies aur frogs mein.

This intermediate feeding stage is followed by a transformation into the adult body, as in butterflies and frogs.

subject: Biology
question_english: How do reptiles, birds and mammals nourish their developing embryos, compared with insects and frogs?
question_hinglish: Reptiles, birds aur mammals apne developing embryos ko insects aur frogs ke comparison mein kaise nourish karte hain?

question_english: Wind-pollinated grasses release about 5,00,000 to 10,00,000 pollen grains per flower and form about 50 to 200 seeds, while insect-pollinated sunflower releases about 20,000 to 40,000 pollen grains and forms about 800 to 1,000 seeds. question_hinglish: Wind-pollinated grasses har flower se lagbhag 5,00,000 se 10,00,000 pollen grains chhodte hain aur 50 se 200 seeds banate hain, jabki insect-pollinated sunflower lagbhag 20,000 se 40,000 pollen grains chhodta hai aur 800 se 1,000 seeds banata hai. Average values use karke dono strategies ka pollen-to-seed ratio compare karo.
answer_english:
Wind-pollinated: average pollen = (5,00,000 + 10,00,000)/2 = 7,50,000; average seeds = (50 + 200)/2 = 125.
Ratio = 7,50,000 / 125 = 6,000 pollen grains per seed.
Insect-pollinated: average pollen = (20,000 + 40,000)/2 = 30,000; average seeds = (800 + 1,000)/2 = 900.
Ratio = 30,000 / 900 = about 33 pollen grains per seed.
Insect pollination is far more efficient, needing about 33 pollen grains per seed compared with about 6,000 for wind pollination.

question_english: Why can producing a very large number of pollen grains still be an effective pollination strategy for wind-pollinated plants?

subject: Biology
question_english: In tomato, stamens cover the stigma; in wheat, flowers open after pollination; and in papaya, male and female flowers are borne on different trees. Which type of pollination is likely in each?
question_hinglish: Tomato mein stamens stigma ko dhak lete hain; wheat mein flowers pollination ke baad khulte hain; aur papaya mein male aur female flowers alag trees pe hote hain. Har ek mein kaun sa pollination likely hai?
answer_english: Tomato: self-pollination, because the stamens cover the stigma so pollen falls on the same flower. Wheat: self-pollination, because pollination happens before the flower opens. Papaya: cross-pollination, because male and female flowers are on different trees, so pollen must travel from one plant to another.
answer_hinglish: Tomato: self-pollination, kyunki stamens stigma ko dhak lete hain toh pollen usi flower pe girta hai. subject: Biology
question_english: Describe the parts of the human male reproductive system and their functions.
question_hinglish: Human male reproductive system ke parts aur unke functions describe karo.
answer_english: Sperm are produced in two oval-shaped testes, present in a pouch of skin called the scrotum, which keeps them slightly cooler than body temperature. The testes also produce a hormone that controls sperm production and causes changes in boys at puberty. Sperm travel through the vas deferens, which opens into the urethra, a common passage for urine and sperm. Seminal vesicles and the prostate add fluids that nourish the sperm and help them stay active and move.

Seminal vesicles aur prostate fluids add karte hain jo sperm ko nourish karte hain aur unhe active rakhte hain.

subject: Biology
question_english: Describe the parts of the human female reproductive system and their functions.
question_hinglish: Human female reproductive system ke parts aur unke functions describe karo.
answer_english: The female reproductive system has a pair of ovaries, oviducts (fallopian tubes), a uterus and a vagina. Uterus ek bag jaisa structure hai jahan foetus develop hota hai, aur yeh cervix naam ke patle raaste se vagina mein khulta hai.

question_english: What is gametogenesis, and how does it differ in males and females?
question_hinglish: Gametogenesis kya hai, aur yeh males aur females mein kaise alag hota hai?

answer_english: A human zygote has 46 chromosomes. It is formed by the fusion of a sperm and an egg, each having 23 chromosomes, so the original chromosome number is restored.

subject: Biology
question_english: Describe the events from fertilisation to the beginning of pregnancy in humans.
question_hinglish: Humans mein fertilisation se lekar pregnancy shuru hone tak ke events describe karo.
answer_english: If a sperm meets the egg in the oviduct and fuses with it, a zygote is formed. The zygote undergoes a series of mitotic divisions while travelling to the uterus, whose inner lining has become thicker and richer in blood vessels. It then implants into this lining to receive nourishment. This implantation marks the beginning of pregnancy.

Zygote is lining mein implant ho jaata hai aur nourishment leta hai. Yahi implantation pregnancy ki shuruaat hai.

subject: Biology
question_english: What is In-vitro Fertilisation (IVF), and what is India's contribution to its history?
question_hinglish: In-vitro Fertilisation (IVF) kya hai, aur iske history mein India ka kya contribution hai?
answer_english: IVF is a medical technique in which an egg and a sperm are combined outside the female body, usually in a laboratory dish, and the fertilised egg is then implanted in the uterus to begin a possible pregnancy. In 1978, Subhash Mukhopadhyay of Kolkata pioneered India's first test tube baby, Kanupriya Agarwal (nicknamed Durga).
answer_hinglish: IVF ek medical technique hai jisme egg aur sperm ko female body ke bahar, usually lab dish mein, combine kiya jaata hai, aur phir fertilised egg ko uterus mein implant kiya jaata hai taaki pregnancy shuru ho sake. 1978 mein Kolkata ke Subhash Mukhopadhyay ne India ka pehla test tube baby, Kanupriya Agarwal (nickname Durga), paida karne mein pioneering kaam kiya.

In 1978, Subhash Mukhopadhyay of Kolkata pioneered India's first test tube baby.

subject: Biology
question_english: What happens when an egg is not fertilised?
question_hinglish: Jab egg fertilise nahi hota toh kya hota hai?
answer_english: If an egg is not fertilised, it remains viable for about a day and then degenerates. The thickened inner lining of the uterus is no longer needed, so it sheds and leaves the body through the vagina along with some blood. This is called menstruation or a period, and it usually lasts 3 to 7 days.
answer_hinglish: Agar egg fertilise nahi hota, toh woh lagbhag ek din tak viable rehta hai aur phir degenerate ho jaata hai. Uterus ki thick inner lining ki zaroorat nahi rehti, toh woh shed ho jaati hai aur thode blood ke saath vagina se body ke bahar nikal jaati hai. Ise menstruation ya period kehte hain, aur yeh usually 3 se 7 din chalta hai.
ncert_context: If an egg is not fertilised, it remains viable for about a day and then degenerates. The inner lining of the uterus, which became thick and rich with blood vessels to receive and nourish the developing zygote, is no longer needed. So the lining sheds, and along with some blood, it leaves the body through the vagina. This process is called menstruation or a period, and it usually lasts 3 to 7 days.

subject: Biology
question_english: Describe the stages of a typical 28-day menstrual cycle.
question_hinglish: Ek typical 28-din ke menstrual cycle ke stages describe karo.
answer_english:
Day 1-5: Menstruation, shedding of the uterine lining.
Day 6-14: The uterine lining gradually rebuilds and an egg starts maturing in the ovary.
Day 14: Ovulation, the ovary releases a mature egg.
Day 15-28: The uterine lining becomes thicker and rich with blood vessels; if no fertilisation happens, it starts breaking down around day 28 and the cycle repeats.
answer_hinglish:
Day 1-5: Menstruation, yaani uterine lining ka shed hona.
Day 6-14: Uterine lining dheere-dheere phir se banti hai aur ovary mein egg mature hona shuru hota hai.
Day 14: Ovulation, ovary mature egg release karti hai.
Day 15-28: Uterine lining thick aur blood vessels se bharpoor ho jaati hai; agar fertilisation nahi hota, toh lagbhag day 28 pe yeh tootne lagti hai aur cycle repeat hota hai.
ncert_context: The cycle of ovulation, preparation of the uterus and menstruation repeats typically every 21 to 35 days, often around 28 days. In a typical cycle, days 1 to 5 are menstruation; on days 6 to 14 the uterine lining rebuilds while an egg matures; on day 14 ovulation occurs; and on days 15 to 28 the lining thickens. If no fertilisation happens, it breaks down around day 28 and the cycle repeats.

subject: Biology
question_english: Rina's period occurs every 28 days. Her last period began on 5th March. On which date is her next period most likely to begin?

subject: Biology
question_english: Explain why the menstrual cycle stops during pregnancy.
question_hinglish: Explain karo ki pregnancy ke dauraan menstrual cycle kyun ruk jaata hai.
answer_english: During pregnancy, the zygote implants in the thickened inner lining of the uterus to receive nourishment for its development. The lining is needed to protect and nourish the developing baby, so it is not shed, and menstruation does not occur.
answer_hinglish: Pregnancy mein zygote uterus ki thick inner lining mein implant hota hai taaki development ke liye nourishment le sake. Developing baby ko protect aur nourish karne ke liye yeh lining zaroori hai, isliye yeh shed nahi hoti aur menstruation nahi hota.
ncert_context: Menstruation happens when an egg is not fertilised: the thickened, blood-rich inner lining of the uterus is no longer needed and sheds. When fertilisation occurs, however, the zygote travels to the uterus and implants into this inner lining to receive nourishment, which marks the beginning of pregnancy. The uterus protects and nourishes the baby throughout pregnancy.

subject: Biology
question_english: List the hygiene practices to follow during menstruation.
question_hinglish: Menstruation ke dauraan follow karne wali hygiene practices batao.
answer_english:
1. Use menstrual products such as sanitary pads (preferably biodegradable), tampons or menstrual cups.
2. Clean the genital area regularly with water, avoiding soap.
3. Wash hands with soap and water before and after changing a pad.
4. Wrap used pads in newspaper or their wrapper before disposing of them in a bin; do not flush them.
5. Clean reusable pads as instructed and dry them completely.
6. Change pads every 4 to 6 hours, or more often if the flow is heavy.

6. Pads har 4 se 6 ghante mein badlo, ya heavy flow mein aur jaldi.

subject: Biology
question_english: Describe the three trimesters of human pregnancy.
question_hinglish: Human pregnancy ke teen trimesters describe karo.
answer_english: Pregnancy lasts about nine months and is divided into three trimesters. In the first trimester, the fertilised egg develops into an embryo during the first two months and major organs start forming; from about the ninth week it is called a foetus. In the second trimester, the foetus grows bigger and stronger, and the mother can usually feel its movements. In the third trimester, the baby grows rapidly and gets ready for life outside the womb.

Pehle trimester mein pehle do mahino mein fertilised egg embryo banta hai aur major organs banne shuru hote hain; lagbhag nauve hafte se ise foetus kehte hain. Doosre trimester mein foetus bada aur strong hota hai, aur mother usually uski movements feel kar sakti hai. Teesre trimester mein baby tezi se badhta hai aur womb ke bahar ki life ke liye taiyaar hota hai.

subject: Biology
question_english: How does childbirth take place, and what care does a newborn need?
question_hinglish: Childbirth kaise hota hai, aur newborn ko kis care ki zaroorat hoti hai?
answer_english: During childbirth, strong contractions of the muscles of the uterus push the foetus out through the birth canal; if a normal birth is not possible or safe, doctors may use medical or surgical procedures. A newborn needs breastfeeding, which provides complete nutrition and protects against many diseases, and must be kept warm, vaccinated on time and handled gently.
answer_hinglish: Childbirth ke time uterus ke muscles ke strong contractions foetus ko birth canal se bahar dhakelte hain; agar normal birth possible ya safe nahi hai, toh doctors medical ya surgical procedures use kar sakte hain. Newborn ko breastfeeding chahiye, jo complete nutrition deti hai aur kai diseases se bachati hai, aur use garam rakhna, time pe vaccinate karna aur dheere se handle karna zaroori hai.
ncert_context: During childbirth, strong contractions of the muscles of the uterus help push the foetus out through the birth canal. If a normal vaginal birth is not possible or safe, doctors may use medical or surgical procedures to deliver the baby safely. After birth, a baby needs special care. Breastfeeding is essential because a mother's milk provides complete nutrition and protects the infant from many diseases. Newborns must be kept warm, vaccinated on time and handled gently.

question_english: What is the difference between sexual maturity and emotional maturity during adolescence?
question_hinglish: Adolescence ke dauraan sexual maturity aur emotional maturity mein kya difference hai?

Sexually mature hone ka matlab adult responsibilities ke liye ready hona nahi hai.

subject: Biology
question_english: What are Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs)? Give examples and state how their transmission can be prevented.
question_hinglish: Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs) kya hain? Examples do aur batao inka transmission kaise roka ja sakta hai.
answer_english: STIs are infections transmitted from an infected person to an uninfected person through sexual contact. They include gonorrhoea, herpes, syphilis, genital warts and HIV, which can eventually lead to AIDS; some are not curable yet. Using condoms can prevent their transmission.
answer_hinglish: STIs woh infections hain jo sexual contact ke through infected person se uninfected person mein jaate hain. Inme gonorrhoea, herpes, syphilis, genital warts aur HIV aate hain, aur HIV aage chalkar AIDS bana sakta hai; inme se kuch abhi tak curable nahi hain. Condoms use karke inka transmission roka ja sakta hai.
ncert_context: Since sexual activity involves close physical contact, some infections can be transmitted from an infected person to an uninfected person. These are called Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs) and include gonorrhoea, herpes, syphilis, genital warts, and HIV, which can eventually lead to AIDS. Some of these are not curable yet. Using condoms can prevent their transmission and also help prevent pregnancy.

subject: Biology
question_english: Describe the different contraceptive methods used to prevent unwanted pregnancy.
question_hinglish: Unwanted pregnancy rokne ke liye use hone wale alag-alag contraceptive methods describe karo.
answer_english:
1. Barrier methods, such as condoms or vaginal covers, stop sperm from reaching the egg.
2. Oral pills change the release of eggs by altering hormones, though they may have side effects.
3. Intra-Uterine Devices (IUDs), such as copper-T, are placed in the uterus, though they may irritate it.
4. Surgical methods block the vas deferens in males or the fallopian tubes in females so that sperm and egg cannot meet.
answer_hinglish:
1. Barrier methods, jaise condoms ya vaginal covers, sperm ko egg tak pahunchne se rokte hain.
2. Oral pills hormones badal kar eggs ke release ko change karti hain, lekin inke kuch side effects ho sakte hain.
3. Intra-Uterine Devices (IUDs), jaise copper-T, uterus mein lagaye jaate hain, lekin kabhi-kabhi uterus ko irritate kar sakte hain.
4. Surgical methods males mein vas deferens ya females mein fallopian tubes ko block karte hain taaki sperm aur egg mil na sakein.

subject: Biology
question_english: If a couple uses oral contraceptive pills but not condoms, which risks remain and why?
question_hinglish: Agar ek couple oral contraceptive pills use karta hai lekin condoms nahi, toh kaun se risks reh jaate hain aur kyun?
answer_english: The risk of Sexually Transmitted Infections remains. Oral pills only prevent pregnancy by altering hormones and changing the release of eggs; they do not stop the close physical contact through which STIs spread. Condoms act as a barrier and prevent both pregnancy and the transmission of STIs.
answer_hinglish: Sexually Transmitted Infections ka risk reh jaata hai. Oral pills sirf hormones badal kar eggs ke release ko change karke pregnancy rokti hain; yeh us close physical contact ko nahi rokti jisse STIs phailte hain. Condoms barrier ka kaam karte hain aur pregnancy aur STIs ka transmission dono rokte hain.

subject: Biology
question_english: Does a unicellular organism like amoeba or yeast ever grow old, given that it produces almost two identical copies when it divides?
question_hinglish: Amoeba ya yeast jaisa unicellular organism kya kabhi 'budha' hota hai, jabki divide hone pe woh almost do identical copies bana deta hai?
answer_english: When a unicellular organism like amoeba divides, the parent cell itself becomes two nearly identical daughter cells by mitosis, so there is no old parent body left behind to age and die in the usual sense. This is different from multicellular organisms, which have a definite life span in which they are born, grow, mature, reproduce and die.

Unicellular organisms like amoeba and yeast reproduce asexually, and when they divide, they produce almost two identical copies.

question_english: What is biodiversity?
question_hinglish: Biodiversity kya hai?
answer_english: Biodiversity is the immense variety of living organisms on the Earth, from microscopic organisms to giant trees, living in countless forms and habitats.
answer_hinglish: Biodiversity Earth pe living organisms ki bahut badi variety hai, microscopic organisms se lekar giant trees tak, jo anginat forms aur habitats mein rehte hain.

This immense variety of living organisms is known as biodiversity, and it is essential for life on the Earth.

question_english: Why do scientists classify organisms, and how is classification useful?

question_english: What are endemic species? Give examples from India.

question_english: What is a biodiversity hotspot? Name some hotspots that include parts of India.
question_hinglish: Biodiversity hotspot kya hota hai? Kuch hotspots ke naam batao jinme India ke parts aate hain.

question_english: How has the biodiversity we see today evolved?
question_hinglish: Aaj jo biodiversity hum dekhte hain woh kaise evolve hui?
answer_english: Small differences among individuals affected their chances of survival and reproduction by helping them adapt to changed conditions. These differences accumulated over many generations and gave rise to new forms of life. So today's diversity is an outcome of continuous changes over a vast span of time, shaped by interactions between organisms and their surroundings.
answer_hinglish: Individuals ke beech chhote differences ne badli hui conditions mein adapt karne mein help karke unke survival aur reproduction ke chances ko affect kiya. Yeh differences kai generations mein jama hote gaye aur nayi forms of life ban gayi. Isliye aaj ki diversity bahut lambe time mein hue lagataar changes ka result hai, jo organisms aur unke surroundings ke interactions se bani.

question_english: How do ancient Indian traditions like Sangam Tinai and sacred groves relate to ecology?
question_hinglish: Sangam Tinai aur sacred groves jaisi ancient Indian traditions ecology se kaise judi hain?
answer_english: The Sangam Tinai classification of landscapes and the protection of sacred groves show a sophisticated literary and cultural understanding of landscapes and their biota. These customs effectively preserved locally diverse habitats, in line with modern ecological principles, even though they were not stated as formal ecological theory.
answer_hinglish: Sangam Tinai mein landscapes ka classification aur sacred groves ki protection landscapes aur unke biota ki ek gehri literary aur cultural samajh dikhate hain. The Rigveda and Brihat Samhita also classify animals by habitat and behaviour.

question_english: In the activity of grouping animals from an ecosystem, what do students notice when they change the grouping criterion, and what question does this raise?
question_hinglish: Ecosystem ke animals ko group karne wali activity mein jab students grouping criterion badalte hain toh woh kya notice karte hain, aur isse kaun sa sawaal uthta hai?
answer_english: Students notice that the same organism can fit into different groups depending on the criterion chosen, such as when it is active or what it eats. answer_hinglish: Students notice karte hain ki ek hi organism alag criterion ke hisaab se alag-alag groups mein fit ho sakta hai, jaise woh kab active hota hai ya kya khata hai. Isse sawaal uthta hai ki scientists kaise decide karte hain ki living organisms ko group karne ke liye kaun se features use karein, aur yahi classification ka idea hai.
ncert_context: In Activity 12.1, students observe animals in an ecosystem picture, record where they are seen and whether they are active by day or night, and then group the same organisms in more than one way, changing the criterion each time, such as grouping eagle, tiger and leopard as carnivores by eating habits. They notice that the same organism can fit into different groups depending on the criterion chosen.

subject: Biology
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification
question_english: List the criteria scientists use to classify living organisms.
question_hinglish: Scientists living organisms ko classify karne ke liye kaun se criteria use karte hain?
answer_english:
1. External features such as shape, size and body organisation.
2. Mode of nutrition, autotrophic or heterotrophic.
3. Internal structures such as skeletal patterns, organs and tissues.
4. Cell structure: unicellular or multicellular, eukaryote or prokaryote, presence or absence of a cell wall.
5. Ecological role: producer, consumer or decomposer.
6. Reproduction: asexual and/or sexual.
7. Genetic similarity, studied using DNA.
answer_hinglish:
1. External features jaise shape, size aur body organisation.
2. Mode of nutrition, autotrophic ya heterotrophic.
3. Internal structures jaise skeletal patterns, organs aur tissues.
4. Cell structure: unicellular ya multicellular, eukaryote ya prokaryote, cell wall hai ya nahi.
5. Ecological role: producer, consumer ya decomposer.
6. Reproduction: asexual aur/ya sexual.
7. Genetic similarity, jo DNA se study ki jaati hai.

Criteria include external features like shape, size and body organisation; mode of nutrition; internal structures such as skeletal patterns, organs and tissues; cell structure, including number of cells, cell type and presence of a cell wall; ecological role as producer, consumer or decomposer; reproduction; and genetic similarity studied using DNA.

question_english: How does the example of a library explain the need for classification?
question_hinglish: Library ka example classification ki zaroorat ko kaise explain karta hai?

Similarly, the Earth has millions of organisms, and classifying them systematically helps us understand them better.

Therefore, classifying these organisms systematically helps us understand them better.

question_english: What is biological classification?
question_hinglish: Biological classification kya hai?
answer_english: Biological classification is the scientific system of grouping living organisms based on their similarities and/or differences, in order to organise information, understand relationships among organisms and study life systematically.

This grouping helps to organise information, understand relationships among organisms and study life in a systematic manner. This scientific system is known as biological classification.

question_english: What was the two kingdom system of classification, and what problem did it create?
question_hinglish: Two kingdom system of classification kya tha, aur isse kya problem hui?

The problem was where to place organisms like Amoeba, Paramecium and bacteria; Amoeba and Paramecium move like animals but are unicellular and heterotrophic, while plants and animals are multicellular.

Problem yeh thi ki Amoeba, Paramecium aur bacteria jaise organisms ko kahan rakhein; Amoeba aur Paramecium animals ki tarah move karte hain par unicellular aur heterotrophic hain, jabki plants aur animals multicellular hote hain.

question_english: Why do classification systems keep changing, and what does this show about how science works?

subject: Biology
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification
question_english: If all unicellular organisms were grouped into a single kingdom, what problems would arise?
question_hinglish: Agar saare unicellular organisms ko ek hi kingdom mein group kar diya jaaye, toh kya problems aayengi?
answer_english: Unicellular organisms differ in fundamental ways. Bacteria are prokaryotes without a true nucleus, while organisms like Amoeba and Paramecium are eukaryotes with a membrane-bound nucleus, and yeast has a chitin cell wall like fungi. Grouping them together would ignore these differences in cell type and cell structure and hide their actual relationships.
answer_hinglish: Unicellular organisms basic tarikon se alag hote hain. Bacteria prokaryotes hain jinme true nucleus nahi hota, jabki Amoeba aur Paramecium jaise organisms eukaryotes hain jinme membrane-bound nucleus hota hai, aur yeast mein fungi jaisi chitin wali cell wall hoti hai. Inhe ek saath group karne se cell type aur cell structure ke yeh differences ignore ho jaayenge aur unke asli relationships chhup jaayenge.
ncert_context: As microscopes improved, scientists noticed that an amoeba has a true, membrane-bound nucleus but bacteria do not. Since both are unicellular but very different, bacteria were placed in a separate kingdom, Monera, while unicellular eukaryotes were placed in Protista. Yeast is unicellular but, since its cell wall is made of chitin, it is placed under fungi. Classification aims to reflect similarities, differences and relationships.

answer_english: Cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) were among the first organisms to produce oxygen through photosynthesis. About 2.5 billion years ago, the oxygen they produced accumulated in the atmosphere and made the Earth suitable for other forms of life. Their fossils, found in stromatolites in Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh, are some of the earliest evidence of life.
answer_hinglish: Cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) photosynthesis se oxygen banane wale pehle organisms mein se the. Lagbhag 2.5 billion saal pehle unki banayi oxygen atmosphere mein jama hui aur Earth doosri forms of life ke liye suitable bani. Inke fossils Rajasthan aur Madhya Pradesh ke stromatolites mein mile hain, jo life ke sabse purane evidence mein se hain.

question_english: Who is known as the 'Father of Modern Biogas' and what did he do?
question_hinglish: 'Father of Modern Biogas' kise kaha jaata hai aur unhone kya kiya?

question_english: Describe the characteristics of Kingdom Protista and the ecological role of protists.
question_hinglish: Kingdom Protista ki characteristics aur protists ka ecological role describe karo.
answer_english: Protista includes single-celled eukaryotic organisms, without a cell wall or with a cell wall made of cellulose, that live in water or moist places. question_english: How is a hay infusion prepared to observe protists?
question_hinglish: Protists dekhne ke liye hay infusion kaise banaya jaata hai?
answer_english:
1. Collect grass after mowing, or straw or fodder.
2. Fill one fourth of a small glass bottle with it.
3. Fill the bottle with stagnant or pond water and mix.
4. Cover it with muslin cloth tied with thread and keep it undisturbed for a week.
5. Take a drop of water with a dropper, place it on a slide and observe under a microscope. Wear a lab coat, mask and gloves, and discard the infusion after autoclaving.
answer_hinglish:
1. Mowing ke baad ki grass, ya straw ya fodder collect karo.
2. Ek chhoti glass bottle ko iske saath ek-chauthai bhar do.
3. Bottle mein stagnant ya pond ka paani bhar ke mix karo.
4. Muslin cloth se dhak ke dhaage se baandho aur ek hafte tak chhod do.
5. Dropper se ek boond paani lekar slide pe rakho aur microscope mein dekho. Lab coat, mask aur gloves pehno, aur infusion ko autoclaving ke baad hi phenko.

subject: Biology
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification
question_english: Describe the characteristics of Kingdom Fungi.
question_hinglish: Kingdom Fungi ki characteristics describe karo.
answer_english: Fungi are mostly multicellular eukaryotes with cell walls made of chitin. They do not make their own food and absorb nutrients from dead or decaying matter through fine filaments that form a network called mycelium. Most are saprophytes and act as decomposers; some are symbiotic and some are parasites. They reproduce sexually and asexually, often by spores, and grow best in warm, moist conditions.
answer_hinglish: Fungi zyada tar multicellular eukaryotes hain jinki cell walls chitin ki bani hoti hain. Yeh apna khana khud nahi banate aur dead ya decaying matter se fine filaments ke through nutrients absorb karte hain, jo milkar mycelium naam ka network banate hain. Zyada tar saprophytes hain aur decomposers ka kaam karte hain; kuch symbiotic aur kuch parasites hote hain. Yeh sexually aur asexually, aksar spores se, reproduce karte hain aur garam, moist conditions mein sabse achha grow karte hain.
ncert_context: Fungi are mostly multicellular eukaryotes with cell walls made of chitin. They do not make their own food. They absorb nutrients from dead or decaying matter through fine filaments that together form a network known as mycelium. Most fungi are saprophytes and play a very important role as decomposers. Some establish symbiotic relationships, while others are parasites. They reproduce both sexually and asexually, often by spores, and grow best in warm, moist conditions.

subject: Biology

question_english: What are lichens, and why are they called natural bioindicators?
question_hinglish: Lichens kya hote hain, aur inhe natural bioindicators kyun kehte hain?
answer_english: Lichens are symbiotic associations of two organisms: an autotrophic alga and a heterotrophic fungus. The fungal partner provides protection, and the algal partner photosynthesises and provides food. Lichens change their colour with air pollutants, so researchers can find the concentration of pollutants from their colour, which makes them natural bioindicators of air quality.
answer_hinglish: Lichens do organisms ka symbiotic association hain: ek autotrophic alga aur ek heterotrophic fungus. Fungal partner protection deta hai, aur algal partner photosynthesis karke khana deta hai. Lichens air pollutants ke saath apna colour badalte hain, toh unke colour se researchers air mein pollutants ki concentration pata kar sakte hain, isliye yeh air quality ke natural bioindicators hain.
ncert_context: White-green patches on tree trunks, damp walls or stones are lichens, which villagers recognise as an indicator of a pollution-free environment. Lichens change their colour with air pollutants, so researchers can find out the concentration of pollutants in the air, making them natural bioindicators of air quality. Biologically, they are symbiotic: one partner is an autotrophic alga and the other a heterotrophic fungus.

Kingdom Plantae is further divided into five classes: Thallophyta, Bryophyta, Pteridophyta, Gymnosperms and Angiosperms.

question_english: Describe the features of Bryophyta with examples.
question_hinglish: Bryophyta ke features examples ke saath describe karo.
answer_english: Bryophytes, such as mosses, liverworts and Marchantia, represent an important shift from water to land. They have a more differentiated body than thallophytes, with root-like rhizoids and simple stem-like and leaf-like structures, but no true roots, stems or leaves and no vascular tissue. They grow in moist, shady places as green mats and need water for reproduction.

Yeh moist, shady jagahon mein green mats ki tarah ugte hain aur reproduction ke liye paani chahiye.

question_english: Why are bryophytes called the amphibians of the plant kingdom?

question_english: Trace how plant groups from algae to angiosperms show structural changes that help them meet the challenges of life on land.
question_hinglish: Algae se angiosperms tak plant groups mein kaise structural changes aaye jo unhe zameen pe life ke challenges face karne mein help karte hain, trace karo.
answer_english: Early plants like algae relied on water for support and reproduction. Bryophytes began to colonise moist land but lacked vascular tissue and needed water for reproduction. Pteridophytes developed true roots, stems, leaves and vascular tissues but still needed water for reproduction. Gymnosperms produced seeds and did not need water for fertilisation. Angiosperms developed flowers and fruits for efficient reproduction and seed dispersal.

Pteridophytes mein true roots, stems, leaves aur vascular tissues aaye, par reproduction ke liye paani abhi bhi chahiye tha. Gymnosperms ne seeds banaye aur fertilisation ke liye paani ki zaroorat khatam hui. Angiosperms mein efficient reproduction aur seed dispersal ke liye flowers aur fruits aaye.

question_english: What is Hortus Malabaricus and why is it significant?
question_hinglish: Hortus Malabaricus kya hai aur yeh significant kyun hai?

subject: Biology

question_english: How would a scientist justify choosing cellular organisation as a more fundamental basis for classification than the presence of xylem and phloem?
question_hinglish: Scientist kaise justify karega ki classification ke liye cellular organisation xylem aur phloem ki presence se zyada fundamental basis hai?
answer_english: Cellular organisation, such as prokaryote or eukaryote, unicellular or multicellular, and presence of a cell wall, applies to all living organisms and is used to separate the five kingdoms. Xylem and phloem are found only in some plant groups, such as pteridophytes, gymnosperms and angiosperms, so they can only distinguish groups within Plantae.
answer_hinglish: Cellular organisation, jaise prokaryote ya eukaryote, unicellular ya multicellular, aur cell wall hai ya nahi, saare living organisms pe apply hoti hai aur five kingdoms ko alag karne mein use hoti hai. Xylem aur phloem sirf kuch plant groups mein hote hain, jaise pteridophytes, gymnosperms aur angiosperms, toh inse sirf Plantae ke andar ke groups hi alag kiye ja sakte hain.
ncert_context: The five kingdom classification is based on cell type (prokaryote or eukaryote), cell structure (presence or absence of a cell wall), level of organisation (unicellular or multicellular) and mode of nutrition. Within Kingdom Plantae, vascular tissues, xylem and phloem, are present in pteridophytes, gymnosperms and angiosperms, but absent in thallophytes and bryophytes.

question_english: Describe the features of Porifera.
question_hinglish: Porifera ke features describe karo.
answer_english: Porifera, or sponges, represent one of the simplest animal body plans. They are multicellular but lack organisation of tissues and organs. Numerous pores in their body let water flow through continuously, bringing food particles and oxygen directly to individual cells and carrying waste away. Sponges remain fixed in one place in aquatic environments.
answer_hinglish: Porifera, yaani sponges, sabse simple animal body plans mein se hain. Yeh multicellular hote hain lekin inme tissues aur organs ka organisation nahi hota. Inke body ke bahut saare pores se paani lagataar behta hai, jo khane ke particles aur oxygen seedha cells tak laata hai aur waste bahar le jaata hai. Sponges aquatic environments mein ek jagah fixed rehte hain.

question_english: What is binomial nomenclature and why is it needed?
question_hinglish: Binomial nomenclature kya hai aur iski zaroorat kyun hai?
answer_english: Binomial nomenclature is a universal system of naming organisms, introduced by Carolus Linnaeus in the 18th century, in which every organism has a two-part scientific name in Latin or Latinised form. It is needed because organisms have different common names in different languages, like bagh, puli, tiger and tigre for the tiger, which can cause confusion.
answer_hinglish: Binomial nomenclature organisms ko naam dene ka universal system hai, jise 18th century mein Carolus Linnaeus ne introduce kiya, jisme har organism ka Latin ya Latinised form mein do parts wala scientific naam hota hai. Iski zaroorat isliye hai kyunki alag languages mein organisms ke alag common naam hote hain, jaise tiger ko bagh, puli, tiger aur tigre kehte hain, jisse confusion ho sakta hai.
ncert_context: A tiger is called bagh in Hindi, puli in Tamil, tiger in English and tigre in French. If people from different regions discuss this animal, confusion may arise. question_english: How did the Purple Frog get its scientific name, and why was its discovery important?
question_hinglish: Purple Frog ko uska scientific naam kaise mila, aur uski discovery important kyun thi?
answer_english: The Purple Frog, Nasikabatrachus sahyadrensis, from Kerala, has a species name after the Sahyadri Hills, its place of discovery. It lives underground for most of the year and comes out only in the monsoon to breed. Its discovery in 2003 helped scientists understand ancient amphibian groups and highlighted the need for biodiversity conservation in the Western Ghats.

question_english: What is the three domain system and on what basis was it proposed?
question_hinglish: Three domain system kya hai aur yeh kis basis pe propose kiya gaya?

subject: Biology
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification
question_english: Why are viruses not placed in any of the five kingdoms?
question_hinglish: Viruses ko five kingdoms mein se kisi mein bhi kyun nahi rakha gaya?
answer_english: Viruses contain genetic material but are acellular, meaning they lack cellular organisation, and they remain inactive outside a host cell. The five kingdoms are based on cell type, cell structure and level of organisation, so viruses do not fit into any kingdom. This shows a limitation of classification systems.
answer_hinglish: Viruses mein genetic material hota hai lekin woh acellular hote hain, yaani unme cellular organisation nahi hota, aur host cell ke bahar woh inactive rehte hain. Five kingdoms cell type, cell structure aur level of organisation pe based hain, isliye viruses kisi kingdom mein fit nahi hote. Isse classification systems ki ek limitation dikhti hai.
ncert_context: The five kingdom classification groups organisms using cell type (prokaryote or eukaryote), cell structure (cell wall), level of organisation (unicellular or multicellular) and mode of nutrition. Viruses, viroids and prions are acellular infectious agents with no cells. Viruses are composed of genetic material with a protein coat. In a case study, an acellular organism containing genetic material and inactive outside a host cell does not fit into any of the five kingdoms.

subject: Biology
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification
question_english: In a case study, organism P is microscopic with no true nucleus, a rigid cell covering, and survives high salinity and temperature; organism Q is multicellular and filamentous, with a cell wall, no chlorophyll, and grows on dead organic matter. Classify P and Q.
question_hinglish: Ek case study mein organism P microscopic hai, isme true nucleus nahi hai, rigid cell covering hai aur yeh high salinity aur temperature jhel leta hai; organism Q multicellular aur filamentous hai, isme cell wall hai, chlorophyll nahi hai aur yeh dead organic matter pe ugta hai. P aur Q ko classify karo.
answer_english: Organism P belongs to Kingdom Monera, because it has no true nucleus, which makes it a prokaryote, and Monera includes unicellular prokaryotes found even in extreme environments. Organism Q belongs to Kingdom Fungi, because it is multicellular and filamentous with a cell wall, lacks chlorophyll and grows on dead organic matter as a decomposer.
answer_hinglish: Organism P Kingdom Monera ka hai, kyunki isme true nucleus nahi hai, yaani yeh prokaryote hai, aur Monera mein extreme environments mein bhi rehne wale unicellular prokaryotes aate hain. Organism Q Kingdom Fungi ka hai, kyunki yeh multicellular aur filamentous hai, isme cell wall hai, chlorophyll nahi hai aur yeh decomposer ki tarah dead organic matter pe ugta hai.
ncert_context: Kingdom Monera includes single-celled prokaryotes without a true nucleus, such as bacteria, which are found everywhere, including hot springs and other extreme environments. Kingdom Fungi includes mostly multicellular eukaryotes with cell walls of chitin; they do not make their own food and absorb nutrients from dead or decaying matter through fine filaments that form a mycelium.

subject: Biology
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification
question_english: Organism R is unicellular with a true nucleus and a contractile vacuole, moves using flagella, and is photosynthetic in light but heterotrophic in the absence of light. Organism Q is multicellular, filamentous, with a cell wall and no chlorophyll. Both are eukaryotic, so why are they placed in different kingdoms?
question_hinglish: Organism R unicellular hai, isme true nucleus aur contractile vacuole hai, yeh flagella se move karta hai, aur light mein photosynthesis karta hai lekin light na hone pe heterotrophic hota hai. answer_english: They differ in level of organisation and cell structure. R is unicellular, so it belongs to Protista, which includes single-celled eukaryotes, some autotrophic and some heterotrophic. Q is multicellular with a cell wall and absorbs nutrients from dead matter, so it belongs to Fungi.
answer_hinglish: Inka level of organisation aur cell structure alag hai. R unicellular hai, isliye yeh Protista mein aata hai, jisme single-celled eukaryotes hote hain, kuch autotrophic aur kuch heterotrophic. Q multicellular hai, isme cell wall hai aur yeh dead matter se nutrients absorb karta hai, isliye yeh Fungi mein aata hai.
ncert_context: The five kingdom classification uses cell type, cell structure, level of organisation and mode of nutrition. Kingdom Protista includes single-celled eukaryotes without a cell wall or with a cellulose cell wall, some autotrophic and some heterotrophic. Kingdom Fungi includes mostly multicellular eukaryotes with cell walls of chitin that do not make their own food and absorb nutrients from dead or decaying matter.

subject: Biology

question_english: What are fossils and how do they serve as evidence of changing biodiversity?
question_hinglish: Fossils kya hote hain aur yeh badalti biodiversity ka evidence kaise dete hain?
answer_english: Fossils are preserved remains of plants and animals found in layers of rocks, sand and mud. Generally, older layers contain simpler organisms while newer layers show more complex forms, so fossils act as natural records of how life has changed over millions of years.
answer_hinglish: Fossils plants aur animals ke preserved remains hain jo rocks, sand aur mud ki layers mein milte hain. Generally purani layers mein simple organisms aur nayi layers mein zyada complex forms milte hain, isliye fossils natural records ki tarah dikhate hain ki millions of saalon mein life kaise badli.
ncert_context: When we talk of diversity changing over time, fossils provide evidence. Fossils are preserved remains of plants and animals found in layers of rocks, sand and mud. Generally, older layers contain simpler organisms, while newer layers show more complex forms. From giant dinosaurs to early humans and ancient plants, important fossils have been discovered in India. Fossils act as natural records of how life has changed over millions of years.

subject: Biology

question_english: Who was Birbal Sahni and what was his contribution?
question_hinglish: Birbal Sahni kaun the aur unka contribution kya tha?
answer_english: Birbal Sahni was an eminent scientist who studied fossil plants. He founded the Birbal Sahni Institute of Palaeosciences in Lucknow, which continues work on ancient plants and past environments. His studies linked present-day plants with their ancestors and showed that life on the Earth has a long, connected history.
answer_hinglish: Birbal Sahni ek prasiddh scientist the jinhone fossil plants ki study ki. Unhone Lucknow mein Birbal Sahni Institute of Palaeosciences ki sthapna ki, jo aaj bhi ancient plants aur past environments pe kaam karta hai. Unki studies ne aaj ke plants ko unke ancestors se joda aur dikhaya ki Earth pe life ka ek lamba, juda hua itihaas hai.
ncert_context: Birbal Sahni was an eminent scientist who studied fossil plants. He founded the Birbal Sahni Institute of Palaeosciences (BSIP) in Lucknow, which continues his work on ancient plants and past environments even today. His studies helped link present-day plants with their ancestors and showed that life on the Earth has a long, connected history. His work continues to inspire young scientists to explore how fossils reveal the story of our planet.

subject: Biology
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification
question_english: Which human activities threaten biodiversity, and what happens when a species disappears?
question_hinglish: Kaun si human activities biodiversity ke liye khatra hain, aur jab ek species khatam ho jaati hai toh kya hota hai?

question_english: What are phumdis, and why is their conservation important for the Sangai deer?
question_hinglish: Phumdis kya hain, aur Sangai deer ke liye inka conservation important kyun hai?
answer_english: Phumdis are floating grasslands in the Loktak lake of Keibul Lamjo National Park, Manipur, made of floating soil beds with rooted vegetation and rich organic matter, a few centimetres to two metres thick. They are home to the endangered Sangai, the dancing deer endemic to Manipur. The phumdis are degenerating, and since the Sangai spends much time there, habitat loss will significantly affect its population.
answer_hinglish: Phumdis Manipur ke Keibul Lamjo National Park ki Loktak lake mein tairti grasslands hain, jo rooted vegetation aur rich organic matter wale floating soil beds se bani hain, aur kuch centimetres se do metre tak thick hoti hain. Yahan Manipur ka endemic, endangered Sangai, yaani dancing deer, rehta hai. Phumdis kharab ho rahi hain, aur kyunki Sangai ka zyada time yahin beet-ta hai, habitat loss se iski population pe bahut asar padega.
ncert_context: Floating grasslands, locally called phumdis, are unique habitats in the Loktak lake of Keibul Lamjo National Park, Manipur. They are home to the endangered Sangai, the dancing deer endemic to Manipur, declared extinct in 1951 and rediscovered in 1953. The phumdis are degenerating, and the Sangai is on the IUCN Red Data list.

subject: Biology
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification
question_english: If you find a new organism in a pond, what features would you observe to classify it, and why?
question_hinglish: Agar tumhe pond mein ek naya organism mile, toh use classify karne ke liye tum kaun se features observe karoge, aur kyun?
answer_english: I would observe whether it is prokaryotic or eukaryotic (has a true nucleus or not), whether it is unicellular or multicellular, whether it has a cell wall, and whether it is autotrophic or heterotrophic. These are the criteria of the five kingdom classification, and together they would place it in the right kingdom; external features and body organisation would then help place it in smaller groups.
answer_hinglish: Main dekhunga ki yeh prokaryotic hai ya eukaryotic (true nucleus hai ya nahi), unicellular hai ya multicellular, isme cell wall hai ya nahi, aur yeh autotrophic hai ya heterotrophic. Yeh five kingdom classification ke criteria hain, aur inse organism sahi kingdom mein jaayega; phir external features aur body organisation se use chhote groups mein rakha ja sakta hai.
ncert_context: The five kingdom classification uses cell type (prokaryote or eukaryote), cell structure (presence or absence of a cell wall), level of organisation (unicellular or multicellular) and mode of nutrition (autotrophic or heterotrophic). Scientists first look at broad features and then at more detailed ones, such as external features, internal structures, ecological role, reproduction and genetic similarity.

subject: Biology
question_english: Why is visible movement not enough to decide whether something is alive?
question_hinglish: Kuch alive hai ya nahi, yeh decide karne ke liye visible movement kaafi kyun nahi hai?
answer_english: A plant that is not visibly growing is still alive, and some animals can breathe without visible movement. So visible movement cannot be the defining characteristic of life. Biologists consider invisible molecular movements to be necessary for life.
answer_hinglish: Jo plant visibly grow nahi kar raha woh bhi alive hota hai, aur kuch animals bina visible movement ke saans le sakte hain. Isliye visible movement life ki defining characteristic nahi ho sakti. Biologists maante hain ki life ke liye invisible molecular movements zaroori hain.
ncert_context: We tend to think of some sort of movement, either growth-related or not, as common evidence for being alive. But a plant that is not visibly growing is still alive, and some animals can breathe without visible movement. So using visible movement as the defining characteristic of life is not enough. Movements over very small scales, like movements of molecules, are invisible to the naked eye, and biologists say these are necessary for life.

question_english: Why are molecular movements necessary for life?

So organisms must keep repairing and maintaining their structures, and since these are made of molecules, they must move molecules around all the time.

subject: Biology
question_english: Why is diffusion insufficient to meet the oxygen requirements of multicellular organisms like humans?
question_hinglish: Humans jaise multicellular organisms ki oxygen requirements diffusion se poori kyun nahi ho sakti?
answer_english: In a single-celled organism, the entire surface is in contact with the environment, so diffusion is enough. In multicellular organisms, all cells are not in direct contact with the surrounding environment, so simple diffusion cannot meet the needs of all cells. It is estimated that diffusion would take 3 years to move an oxygen molecule from our lungs to our toes.
answer_hinglish: Single-celled organism ki poori surface environment ke contact mein hoti hai, toh diffusion kaafi hai. Multicellular organisms mein saare cells environment ke direct contact mein nahi hote, isliye simple diffusion saare cells ki zaroorat poori nahi kar sakta. Estimate hai ki diffusion se ek oxygen molecule ko lungs se toes tak pahunchne mein 3 saal lagenge.

subject: Biology
question_english: Why do multicellular organisms need a transportation system and an excretory system?
question_hinglish: Multicellular organisms ko transportation system aur excretory system ki zaroorat kyun hoti hai?
answer_english: In multicellular organisms, food and oxygen are taken up by specialised tissues at one place, but all parts of the body need them, so a transportation system is needed. Chemical reactions that use food and oxygen produce by-products that are useless or even harmful, so they must be removed by excretion, and the transport system must carry these wastes to the excretory tissue.
answer_hinglish: Multicellular organisms mein khana aur oxygen specialised tissues ek jagah lete hain, lekin body ke saare parts ko inki zaroorat hoti hai, isliye transportation system chahiye. Khana aur oxygen use karne wali chemical reactions aise by-products banati hain jo useless ya harmful hote hain, isliye unhe excretion se nikalna padta hai, aur transport system ko yeh wastes excretory tissue tak le jaane padte hain.

subject: Biology
question_english: Differentiate between autotrophic and heterotrophic nutrition.
question_hinglish: Autotrophic aur heterotrophic nutrition mein difference batao.
answer_english: Autotrophs, such as green plants and some bacteria, use simple food material from inorganic sources, carbon dioxide and water, and make their own food using an external energy source like the Sun. Heterotrophs, such as animals and fungi, take in complex substances prepared by other organisms and break them down using enzymes, so they depend directly or indirectly on autotrophs.
answer_hinglish: Autotrophs, jaise green plants aur kuch bacteria, inorganic sources, yaani carbon dioxide aur paani, se simple food material lete hain aur Sun jaise external energy source se apna khana khud banate hain. Heterotrophs, jaise animals aur fungi, doosre organisms ke banaye complex substances lete hain aur enzymes se unhe todte hain, isliye woh directly ya indirectly autotrophs pe depend karte hain.

question_english: What is photosynthesis? Write its balanced equation.
question_hinglish: Photosynthesis kya hai? Iski balanced equation likho.

6CO2 + 12H2O --(chlorophyll, sunlight)--> C6H12O6 (glucose) + 6O2 + 6H2O

subject: Biology
question_english: What are the events that occur during photosynthesis?
question_hinglish: Photosynthesis ke dauraan kaun se events hote hain?
answer_english:
(i) Absorption of light energy by chlorophyll.
(ii) Conversion of light energy to chemical energy and splitting of water molecules into hydrogen and oxygen.
(iii) Reduction of carbon dioxide to carbohydrates.
answer_hinglish:
(i) Chlorophyll dwara light energy ka absorption.
(ii) Light energy ka chemical energy mein conversion aur water molecules ka hydrogen aur oxygen mein splitting.
(iii) Carbon dioxide ka carbohydrates mein reduction.

These steps need not take place one after the other immediately. For example, desert plants take up carbon dioxide at night and prepare an intermediate which is acted upon by energy absorbed by chlorophyll during the day.

subject: Biology
question_english: What happens to carbohydrates that are not used immediately by the plant? What is the equivalent in humans?
question_hinglish: Jo carbohydrates plant turant use nahi karta unka kya hota hai? Humans mein iska equivalent kya hai?
answer_english: Carbohydrates not used immediately are stored as starch, which serves as the plant's internal energy reserve to be used when required. In humans, some of the energy derived from food is similarly stored in the body in the form of glycogen.
answer_hinglish: Jo carbohydrates turant use nahi hote, woh starch ke roop mein store ho jaate hain, jo plant ka internal energy reserve hai aur zaroorat pe use hota hai. Humans mein bhi khane se mili kuch energy body mein glycogen ke roop mein store hoti hai.
ncert_context: Carbohydrates produced by photosynthesis are utilised for providing energy to the plant. The carbohydrates which are not used immediately are stored in the form of starch, which serves as the internal energy reserve to be used as and when required by the plant. A somewhat similar situation is seen in us, where some of the energy derived from the food we eat is stored in our body in the form of glycogen.

subject: Biology
question_english: How do guard cells control the opening and closing of stomata, and why do plants close them?
question_hinglish: Guard cells stomata ko kaise kholte aur band karte hain, aur plants inhe band kyun karte hain?
answer_english: The guard cells swell when water flows into them, causing the stomatal pore to open, and the pore closes when the guard cells shrink. Since large amounts of water can be lost through stomata, the plant closes them when it does not need carbon dioxide for photosynthesis.
answer_hinglish: Jab guard cells mein paani jaata hai toh woh phool jaate hain aur stomatal pore khul jaata hai, aur guard cells sikudne pe pore band ho jaata hai. Stomata se bahut saara paani nikal sakta hai, isliye plant inhe tab band kar deta hai jab use photosynthesis ke liye carbon dioxide ki zaroorat nahi hoti.
ncert_context: Stomata are tiny pores on the surface of leaves through which massive amounts of gaseous exchange take place for photosynthesis, though gases are also exchanged across the surface of stems, roots and leaves. Since large amounts of water can also be lost through stomata, the plant closes these pores when it does not need carbon dioxide. The opening and closing of the pore is a function of the guard cells, which swell or shrink.

question_english: Where do plants get each of the raw materials required for photosynthesis and for building their body?
question_hinglish: Plants photosynthesis aur body banane ke liye zaroori har raw material kahan se lete hain?

subject: Biology
question_english: What are peristaltic movements?
question_hinglish: Peristaltic movements kya hote hain?
answer_english: Peristaltic movements are the rhythmic contractions of the muscles lining the alimentary canal that push the food forward in a regulated manner. They occur all along the gut.
answer_hinglish: Peristaltic movements alimentary canal ki lining ke muscles ke rhythmic contractions hain jo khane ko regulated tarike se aage dhakelte hain. Yeh poore gut mein hote hain.
ncert_context: It is necessary to move food in a regulated manner along the digestive tube so that it can be processed properly in each part. The lining of the canal has muscles that contract rhythmically in order to push the food forward. These peristaltic movements occur all along the gut, from the mouth through the oesophagus, stomach and intestines.

subject: Biology
question_english: What do the gastric glands secrete and what is the function of each secretion?
question_hinglish: Gastric glands kya secrete karti hain aur har secretion ka kya function hai?
answer_english: Gastric glands in the stomach wall release hydrochloric acid, the protein-digesting enzyme pepsin, and mucus. The hydrochloric acid creates an acidic medium that facilitates the action of pepsin. Pepsin digests proteins. Mucus protects the inner lining of the stomach from the action of the acid.

ncert_context: The stomach is a large organ which expands when food enters it, and its muscular walls mix the food thoroughly with digestive juices. The acid creates an acidic medium which facilitates pepsin's action, and the mucus protects the inner lining of the stomach from the acid under normal conditions.

subject: Biology
question_english: How are fats digested in our body, and where does this take place?
question_hinglish: Hamari body mein fats kaise digest hote hain, aur yeh kahan hota hai?
answer_english: Fats are digested in the small intestine. Fats are present as large globules, so bile salts from the liver break them into smaller globules (emulsification), increasing the efficiency of enzyme action. Lipase in pancreatic juice then breaks down the emulsified fats, and enzymes in intestinal juice finally convert fats into fatty acids and glycerol.
answer_hinglish: Fats small intestine mein digest hote hain. Fats bade globules ke roop mein hote hain, toh liver ke bile salts unhe chhote globules mein tod dete hain (emulsification), jisse enzymes better kaam kar paate hain. Phir pancreatic juice ka lipase emulsified fats ko todta hai, aur intestinal juice ke enzymes aakhir mein fats ko fatty acids aur glycerol mein badal dete hain.

Bile salts break them into smaller globules, increasing the efficiency of enzyme action, similar to the emulsifying action of soaps on dirt. Pancreatic juice contains lipase for breaking down emulsified fats, and intestinal juice finally converts fats into fatty acids and glycerol.

subject: Biology
question_english: What is the role of the large intestine and the sphincter muscles in digestion?
question_hinglish: Digestion mein large intestine aur sphincter muscles ka kya role hai?
answer_english: The unabsorbed food is sent into the large intestine, whose walls absorb more water from it, and the rest is removed through the anus. The exit of food from the stomach into the small intestine is regulated by a sphincter muscle, and the exit of waste is regulated by the anal sphincter.

The rest of the material is removed from the body via the anus, and the exit of this waste is regulated by the anal sphincter.

subject: Biology
question_english: What causes dental caries and how can it be prevented?
question_hinglish: Dental caries kis wajah se hota hai aur ise kaise roka ja sakta hai?
answer_english: Dental caries, or tooth decay, begins when bacteria acting on sugars produce acids that soften or demineralise the enamel and dentine. Masses of bacteria and food particles stick to teeth as dental plaque, which stops saliva from neutralising the acid. Brushing teeth after eating removes the plaque before bacteria produce acids.
answer_hinglish: Dental caries, yaani tooth decay, tab shuru hota hai jab sugars pe kaam karne wale bacteria acids banate hain jo enamel aur dentine ko soft ya demineralise kar dete hain. Bacteria aur food particles daanton pe dental plaque bana dete hain, jisse saliva acid ko neutralise nahi kar paata. Khane ke baad brush karne se plaque bacteria ke acid banane se pehle hi hat jaata hai.

Masses of bacterial cells together with food particles stick to the teeth to form dental plaque. Saliva cannot reach the tooth surface to neutralise the acid as plaque covers the teeth. Brushing after eating removes plaque, and if untreated, microorganisms may invade the pulp.

question_english: What is the function of digestive enzymes?

subject: Biology
question_english: Differentiate between aerobic and anaerobic respiration. Name organisms that use anaerobic respiration.
question_hinglish: Aerobic aur anaerobic respiration mein difference batao. Anaerobic respiration use karne wale organisms ke naam batao.
answer_english: Aerobic respiration takes place in the presence of oxygen in the mitochondria, breaking pyruvate into carbon dioxide and water, and releases a lot more energy. Yeast uses anaerobic respiration.

Yeast anaerobic respiration use karta hai.

In muscle cells lacking oxygen, pyruvate becomes lactic acid.

subject: Biology
question_english: What are the different ways in which glucose is oxidised to provide energy in various organisms?
question_hinglish: Alag-alag organisms mein energy dene ke liye glucose kin-kin tarikon se oxidise hota hai?

subject: Biology
question_english: How is ATP formed during respiration, and how does it provide energy for cellular activities?
question_hinglish: Respiration ke dauraan ATP kaise banta hai, aur yeh cellular activities ke liye energy kaise deta hai?
answer_english: ATP is the molecule made from ADP and inorganic phosphate using the energy released during respiration. When its terminal phosphate linkage is broken using water, energy equivalent to 30.5 kJ/mol is released, which drives endothermic reactions. Like a battery used for many purposes, ATP fuels muscle contraction, protein synthesis, conduction of nerve impulses and other activities, so it is the energy currency.
answer_hinglish: ATP woh molecule hai jo respiration mein nikli energy se ADP aur inorganic phosphate se banta hai. Jab iski terminal phosphate linkage paani se todi jaati hai, toh 30.5 kJ/mol energy release hoti hai, jo endothermic reactions chalati hai. Battery ki tarah jo kai kaamon mein aati hai, ATP muscle contraction, protein synthesis, nerve impulses ke conduction aur doosri activities ko fuel karta hai, isliye yeh energy currency hai.
ncert_context: The energy released during cellular respiration is used to make ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate. Endothermic processes in the cell use ATP to drive reactions. When the terminal phosphate linkage in ATP is broken using water, energy equivalent to 30.5 kJ/mol is released. Just as a battery provides energy for many uses, ATP is used for muscle contraction, protein synthesis, conduction of nervous impulses and many other activities.

subject: Biology
question_english: How does gas exchange take place in plants, and how does it differ between day and night?
question_hinglish: Plants mein gas exchange kaise hota hai, aur din aur raat mein yeh kaise alag hota hai?
answer_english: Plants exchange gases through stomata, and large intercellular spaces ensure all cells are in contact with air; carbon dioxide and oxygen move by diffusion. At night, when there is no photosynthesis, carbon dioxide elimination is the major activity. During the day, the carbon dioxide from respiration is used for photosynthesis, so there is no carbon dioxide release, and oxygen release is the major event.
answer_hinglish: Plants stomata se gases exchange karte hain, aur bade intercellular spaces ensure karte hain ki saare cells hawa ke contact mein rahein; carbon dioxide aur oxygen diffusion se move karte hain. Raat mein photosynthesis nahi hota, toh carbon dioxide nikalna main activity hai. Din mein respiration ki carbon dioxide photosynthesis mein use ho jaati hai, toh CO2 release nahi hoti aur oxygen release main event hota hai.
ncert_context: Plants exchange gases through stomata, and the large intercellular spaces ensure that all cells are in contact with air. Carbon dioxide and oxygen are exchanged by diffusion, and the direction depends on conditions and the plant's needs. At night, with no photosynthesis, CO2 elimination is the major exchange activity. During the day, CO2 generated during respiration is used up for photosynthesis, so there is no CO2 release; oxygen release is the major event.

subject: Biology
question_english: Why do aquatic organisms breathe much faster than terrestrial organisms?
question_hinglish: Aquatic organisms terrestrial organisms se kahin zyada tez saans kyun lete hain?
answer_english: Aquatic animals must use oxygen dissolved in water, and the amount of dissolved oxygen is fairly low compared with the amount of oxygen in air. So the rate of breathing in aquatic organisms is much faster than in terrestrial organisms.
answer_hinglish: Aquatic animals ko paani mein ghuli oxygen use karni padti hai, aur dissolved oxygen ki amount hawa ki oxygen se kaafi kam hoti hai. Isliye aquatic organisms ki breathing rate terrestrial organisms se kahin zyada tez hoti hai.
ncert_context: Terrestrial animals can breathe the oxygen in the atmosphere, but animals that live in water need to use the oxygen dissolved in water. Since the amount of dissolved oxygen is fairly low compared to the amount of oxygen in the air, the rate of breathing in aquatic organisms is much faster than that seen in terrestrial organisms. Fishes take in water through their mouths and force it past the gills.

question_english: How do fishes obtain oxygen?

subject: Biology
question_english: Describe the path of air in the human respiratory system and how the air passage is protected.
question_hinglish: Human respiratory system mein hawa ka raasta describe karo aur batao air passage kaise protected rehta hai.
answer_english: Air enters through the nostrils, where it is filtered by fine hairs and mucus lining the passage. It passes through the throat, which has rings of cartilage that prevent the air passage from collapsing, into the lungs. In the lungs, the passage divides into smaller tubes that end in balloon-like alveoli, where gas exchange takes place.
answer_hinglish: Hawa nostrils se andar aati hai, jahan passage ki lining ke fine hairs aur mucus use filter karte hain. Phir yeh throat se hoti hui lungs mein jaati hai; throat mein cartilage ke rings hote hain jo air passage ko collapse nahi hone dete. subject: Biology
question_english: Describe the mechanism of breathing in humans.
question_hinglish: Humans mein breathing ka mechanism describe karo.
answer_english: When we breathe in, we lift our ribs and flatten our diaphragm, making the chest cavity larger, so air is sucked into the lungs and fills the alveoli. Blood brings carbon dioxide from the body for release into the alveoli, and oxygen from alveolar air is taken up by blood in alveolar blood vessels to be carried to all cells.

subject: Biology
question_english: How are oxygen and carbon dioxide transported in human beings?
question_hinglish: Humans mein oxygen aur carbon dioxide kaise transport hote hain?
answer_english: Oxygen is carried by the respiratory pigment haemoglobin, present in red blood corpuscles, which has a very high affinity for oxygen; it takes up oxygen in the lungs and releases it in tissues deficient in oxygen. Carbon dioxide is more soluble in water than oxygen, so it is mostly transported in dissolved form in the blood.
answer_hinglish: Oxygen ko red blood corpuscles mein maujood respiratory pigment haemoglobin carry karta hai, jiski oxygen ke liye affinity bahut zyada hoti hai; yeh lungs mein oxygen leta hai aur oxygen ki kami wale tissues mein chhod deta hai. Carbon dioxide paani mein oxygen se zyada soluble hai, isliye yeh zyada tar blood mein dissolved form mein transport hoti hai.
ncert_context: When the body size of animals is large, diffusion alone cannot take care of oxygen delivery to all parts of the body. Instead, respiratory pigments take up oxygen from air in the lungs and carry it to tissues deficient in oxygen. In human beings, the respiratory pigment is haemoglobin, which has a very high affinity for oxygen and is present in red blood corpuscles. Carbon dioxide is more soluble in water and is mostly transported dissolved in blood.

subject: Biology
question_english: What are the components of the transport system in human beings and their functions?
question_hinglish: Humans mein transport system ke components kya hain aur unke functions kya hain?
answer_english:
1. Heart: a muscular pump that pushes blood around the body.
2. Blood vessels: arteries carry blood away from the heart, veins bring it back, and capillaries allow exchange with cells.
3. Blood: plasma carries food, carbon dioxide and nitrogenous wastes; RBCs carry oxygen; platelets help clotting.
4. Lymph: carries digested fat and drains excess tissue fluid back into blood.
answer_hinglish:
1. Heart: ek muscular pump jo blood ko body mein dhakelta hai.
2. Blood vessels: arteries heart se blood door le jaati hain, veins wapas laati hain, aur capillaries cells ke saath exchange hone deti hain.
3. Blood: plasma khana, carbon dioxide aur nitrogenous wastes le jaata hai; RBCs oxygen le jaate hain; platelets clotting mein help karte hain.
4. Lymph: digested fat le jaata hai aur extra tissue fluid ko wapas blood mein bhejta hai.
ncert_context: Our transport system needs a pumping organ to push blood around the body, a network of tubes to reach all the tissues, and a system to repair the network if damaged. The heart is the pump; arteries, veins and capillaries are the tubes; and platelets plug leaks by clotting. Blood plasma carries food, CO2 and nitrogenous wastes, and RBCs carry oxygen. Lymph also helps in transportation.

subject: Biology
question_english: Why does the heart have different chambers?
question_hinglish: Heart mein alag-alag chambers kyun hote hain?
answer_english: Both oxygen and carbon dioxide have to be transported by blood, so the heart has different chambers to prevent oxygen-rich blood from mixing with blood containing carbon dioxide.
answer_hinglish: Blood ko oxygen aur carbon dioxide dono transport karne hote hain, isliye heart mein alag chambers hote hain taaki oxygen-rich blood carbon dioxide wale blood se mix na ho.
ncert_context: The heart is a muscular organ about as big as our fist. Because both oxygen and carbon dioxide have to be transported by the blood, the heart has different chambers to prevent the oxygen-rich blood from mixing with the blood containing carbon dioxide. The carbon dioxide-rich blood has to reach the lungs for carbon dioxide removal, and oxygenated blood from the lungs is brought back to the heart and then pumped to the rest of the body.

subject: Biology
question_english: Describe the flow of blood through the four chambers of the human heart.
question_hinglish: Human heart ke chaar chambers mein blood ka flow describe karo.
answer_english: Oxygen-rich blood from the lungs enters the left atrium, which relaxes to collect it and then contracts while the left ventricle relaxes, transferring the blood to it. The muscular left ventricle contracts and pumps blood to the body. Deoxygenated blood from the body enters the right atrium, which contracts to pass it to the right ventricle, which pumps it to the lungs for oxygenation. Valves prevent backflow.
answer_hinglish: Lungs se oxygen-rich blood left atrium mein aata hai, jo relax hokar use collect karta hai aur phir contract hota hai jab left ventricle relax hota hai, toh blood left ventricle mein chala jaata hai. Muscular left ventricle contract hokar blood body ko pump karta hai. Body se deoxygenated blood right atrium mein aata hai, jo contract hokar use right ventricle mein bhejta hai, aur right ventricle use oxygenation ke liye lungs ko pump karta hai. Valves blood ko peeche nahi bahne dete.
ncert_context: Oxygen-rich blood from the lungs comes to the thin-walled left atrium, which relaxes while collecting it, then contracts while the left ventricle relaxes, transferring the blood. When the muscular left ventricle contracts, blood is pumped to the body. Deoxygenated blood from the body comes to the right atrium, which contracts as the right ventricle dilates, and the right ventricle pumps it to the lungs. Valves ensure blood does not flow backwards.
