subject: Biology
question_english: What is double circulation? Why is it necessary in mammals and birds?
question_hinglish: Double circulation kya hai? Mammals aur birds mein yeh zaroori kyun hai?
answer_english: In double circulation, blood passes through the heart twice during each cycle through the body: once to be pumped to the lungs and once to be pumped to the rest of the body. Separating the right and left sides of the heart keeps oxygenated and deoxygenated blood from mixing, allowing a highly efficient oxygen supply. This is needed by birds and mammals, which have high energy needs because they constantly use energy to maintain their body temperature.
answer_hinglish: Double circulation mein body ke har cycle mein blood heart se do baar guzarta hai: ek baar lungs ko pump hone ke liye aur ek baar baaki body ko. Heart ke right aur left side alag hone se oxygenated aur deoxygenated blood mix nahi hota, jisse oxygen ki supply bahut efficient hoti hai. Birds aur mammals ko iski zaroorat hai kyunki body temperature maintain karne mein woh lagataar energy use karte hain, toh unki energy needs zyada hoti hain.
ncert_context: The separation of the right and left sides of the heart keeps oxygenated and deoxygenated blood from mixing, allowing a highly efficient supply of oxygen. This is useful in animals with high energy needs, such as birds and mammals, which constantly use energy to maintain body temperature. In fishes, blood goes through the heart only once per cycle; in other vertebrates, it goes through the heart twice per cycle, which is known as double circulation.

subject: Biology
question_english: Compare the hearts of fishes, amphibians and reptiles, and birds and mammals.
question_hinglish: Fishes, amphibians aur reptiles, aur birds aur mammals ke hearts compare karo.
answer_english: Fishes have a two-chambered heart; blood is pumped to the gills, oxygenated, and passes directly to the body, going through the heart only once per cycle. Amphibians and many reptiles have three-chambered hearts and tolerate some mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood, since their body temperature depends on the environment. Birds and mammals have four chambers with complete separation and double circulation.
answer_hinglish: Fishes ka heart two-chambered hota hai; blood gills ko pump hota hai, wahan oxygenated hota hai aur seedha body mein jaata hai, aur har cycle mein heart se sirf ek baar guzarta hai. Amphibians aur kai reptiles ka heart three-chambered hota hai aur oxygenated aur deoxygenated blood thoda mix hota hai, kyunki unka body temperature environment pe depend karta hai. Birds aur mammals mein chaar chambers hote hain, poora separation aur double circulation.

Fishes have only two chambers; blood is pumped to the gills, oxygenated there, and passes directly to the body, going through the heart only once per cycle. Birds and mammals have separated right and left sides.

subject: Biology
question_english: Differentiate between arteries, veins and capillaries.
question_hinglish: Arteries, veins aur capillaries mein difference batao.
answer_english: Arteries carry blood away from the heart to organs; since blood emerges under high pressure, they have thick, elastic walls. Veins collect blood from organs and bring it back to the heart; they do not need thick walls but have valves so blood flows in one direction. Capillaries are the smallest vessels with walls one cell thick, across which material is exchanged between blood and surrounding cells.
answer_hinglish: Arteries heart se blood organs tak le jaati hain; blood high pressure se nikalta hai isliye inki walls thick aur elastic hoti hain. Veins organs se blood wapas heart tak laati hain; inhe thick walls nahi chahiye lekin inme valves hote hain taaki blood ek hi direction mein bahe. Capillaries sabse chhoti vessels hain jinki walls ek cell thick hoti hain, aur inke through blood aur cells ke beech material ka exchange hota hai.
ncert_context: Arteries carry blood away from the heart to various organs; since blood emerges under high pressure, they have thick, elastic walls. Veins collect blood from organs and bring it back to the heart; they do not need thick walls because the blood is no longer under pressure, but they have valves so blood flows in one direction. Arteries divide into capillaries with one-cell-thick walls, across which exchange occurs; capillaries join to form veins.

subject: Biology
question_english: How do platelets help maintain the circulatory system?
question_hinglish: Platelets circulatory system ko maintain karne mein kaise help karte hain?
answer_english: When we are injured and bleed, loss of blood must be minimised, and leakage would also reduce pressure and the efficiency of the pumping system. Platelets circulate around the body and plug these leaks by helping blood to clot at points of injury.
answer_hinglish: Jab chot lagne se bleeding hoti hai, toh blood ka loss kam karna zaroori hai, aur leakage se pressure bhi ghatega aur pumping system ki efficiency kam hogi. Platelets body mein ghoomte rehte hain aur injury ki jagah blood ko clot karke in leaks ko band kar dete hain.
ncert_context: If the system of blood vessels develops a leak, such as when we are injured and start bleeding, the loss of blood from the system has to be minimised. In addition, leakage would lead to a loss of pressure, which would reduce the efficiency of the pumping system. To avoid this, the blood has platelet cells which circulate around the body and plug these leaks by helping to clot the blood at these points of injury.

subject: Biology
question_english: What is lymph? How is it formed and what are its functions?
question_hinglish: Lymph kya hai? Yeh kaise banta hai aur iske functions kya hain?
answer_english: Lymph, or tissue fluid, forms when some plasma, proteins and blood cells escape through pores in capillary walls into intercellular spaces. It is similar to plasma but colourless and contains less protein. It drains into lymphatic capillaries, which join into lymph vessels that open into larger veins. Lymph carries digested and absorbed fat from the intestine and drains excess fluid from extracellular space back into the blood.
answer_hinglish: Lymph, yaani tissue fluid, tab banta hai jab capillary walls ke pores se kuch plasma, proteins aur blood cells intercellular spaces mein nikal jaate hain. Yeh plasma jaisa hota hai lekin colourless aur kam protein wala. Yeh lymphatic capillaries mein jaata hai, jo milkar lymph vessels banati hain aur badi veins mein khulti hain. Lymph intestine se digested aur absorbed fat le jaata hai aur extra fluid ko wapas blood mein bhejta hai.

subject: Biology
question_english: Why do plants have low energy needs and relatively slow transport systems, yet still need a proper transport system?
question_hinglish: Plants ki energy needs kam kyun hoti hain aur unke transport systems slow kyun hote hain, phir bhi unhe proper transport system kyun chahiye?
answer_english: Plants do not move, and their bodies have a large proportion of dead cells in many tissues, so they have low energy needs and can use relatively slow transport systems. However, in plants like tall trees, the distance between the roots, which absorb raw materials, and the leaves, which make food, is large, so diffusion is not sufficient and a proper transport system is essential.
answer_hinglish: Plants move nahi karte, aur unke kai tissues mein dead cells bahut zyada hote hain, isliye unki energy needs kam hoti hain aur woh slow transport systems use kar sakte hain. ncert_context: If the distances between soil-contacting organs and chlorophyll-containing organs are small, energy and raw materials can diffuse to all parts of the plant. But if these distances become large, diffusion will not be sufficient. Distances can still be very large in tall trees.

subject: Biology
question_english: What is translocation and how does it take place in plants?
question_hinglish: Translocation kya hai aur plants mein yeh kaise hota hai?
answer_english: Translocation is the transport of soluble products of photosynthesis, along with amino acids and other substances, through phloem, in both upward and downward directions in the sieve tubes with the help of companion cells. It uses energy: sucrose is transferred into phloem using ATP, which increases osmotic pressure so water moves in, and this pressure moves material to tissues with lower pressure.
answer_hinglish: Translocation photosynthesis ke soluble products, amino acids aur doosre substances ka phloem ke through transport hai, jo sieve tubes mein companion cells ki help se upar aur neeche dono directions mein hota hai. Isme energy lagti hai: sucrose ko ATP ki energy se phloem mein bheja jaata hai, jisse osmotic pressure badhta hai, paani andar aata hai, aur yeh pressure material ko kam pressure wale tissues tak le jaata hai.
ncert_context: The transport of soluble products of photosynthesis is called translocation and occurs in phloem. Besides these products, phloem transports amino acids and other substances, especially to storage organs of roots, fruits and seeds and to growing organs. Translocation occurs in sieve tubes with the help of companion cells, both upward and downward. Unlike xylem transport, it uses energy: sucrose is transferred into phloem using ATP, increasing osmotic pressure.

subject: Biology
question_english: Describe the structure and functioning of a nephron.
question_hinglish: Nephron ka structure aur functioning describe karo.
answer_english: A nephron is the filtration unit of the kidney. It has a cluster of very thin-walled blood capillaries associated with the cup-shaped end of a coiled tube called Bowman's capsule, which collects the filtrate. As the filtrate flows along the tube, substances like glucose, amino acids, salts and a major amount of water are selectively reabsorbed, and the remaining urine passes into the ureter.
answer_hinglish: Nephron kidney ki filtration unit hai. Isme bahut patli walls wali blood capillaries ka ek cluster hota hai jo ek coiled tube ke cup-shaped end, Bowman's capsule, se juda hota hai, aur yeh capsule filtrate collect karta hai. Filtrate tube mein aage badhte hue glucose, amino acids, salts aur zyada tar paani selectively reabsorb ho jaate hain, aur bachi urine ureter mein jaati hai.
ncert_context: The purpose of making urine is to filter waste products from the blood; nitrogenous wastes like urea or uric acid are removed from blood in the kidneys. The basic filtration unit is a cluster of very thin-walled capillaries associated with the cup-shaped end of a coiled tube called Bowman's capsule, which collects the filtrate. Each kidney has large numbers of these units, called nephrons. Glucose, amino acids, salts and much water are selectively reabsorbed.

subject: Biology
question_english: In a healthy adult, the initial filtrate in the kidneys is about 180 L daily, but only about 1.5 L of urine is excreted. What percentage of the filtrate is reabsorbed?

answer_english:
Given: filtrate = 180 L, urine excreted = 1.5 L.
Step 1: Volume reabsorbed = 180 - 1.5 = 178.5 L.
Step 2: Percentage reabsorbed = (178.5 / 180) x 100 = about 99.2%.
So about 99% of the filtrate is reabsorbed in the kidney tubules.

subject: Biology
question_english: How does an artificial kidney (haemodialysis) work, and how is it different from a natural kidney?
question_hinglish: Artificial kidney (haemodialysis) kaise kaam karti hai, aur yeh natural kidney se kaise alag hai?
answer_english: An artificial kidney contains tubes with a semi-permeable lining suspended in a tank of dialysing fluid, which has the same osmotic pressure as blood but no nitrogenous wastes. The patient's blood passes through the tubes, wastes diffuse into the fluid, and purified blood is pumped back. Unlike the natural kidney, there is no reabsorption.
answer_hinglish: Artificial kidney mein semi-permeable lining wali tubes hoti hain jo dialysing fluid ke tank mein latki hoti hain; is fluid ka osmotic pressure blood jaisa hota hai lekin isme nitrogenous wastes nahi hote. Patient ka blood in tubes se guzarta hai, wastes diffusion se fluid mein chale jaate hain, aur saaf blood wapas pump kar diya jaata hai. Natural kidney ke ulat isme reabsorption nahi hota.
ncert_context: In case of kidney failure, an artificial kidney can be used to remove nitrogenous wastes from blood through dialysis. The patient's blood passes through these tubes, wastes pass into the fluid by diffusion, and purified blood is pumped back. Unlike the kidney, there is no reabsorption.

subject: Biology
question_english: Compare the functioning of alveoli in the lungs and nephrons in the kidneys.
question_hinglish: Lungs ke alveoli aur kidneys ke nephrons ki functioning compare karo.
answer_english: Both have clusters of very thin-walled blood capillaries for exchange. Alveoli are balloon-like structures that provide a large surface for exchange of gases: oxygen enters blood and carbon dioxide leaves it. Nephrons filter nitrogenous wastes like urea from blood into Bowman's capsule, and then selectively reabsorb useful substances like glucose, amino acids, salts and water.

Nephrons urea jaise nitrogenous wastes ko blood se Bowman's capsule mein filter karte hain, aur phir glucose, amino acids, salts aur paani jaise useful substances ko selectively reabsorb karte hain.
ncert_context: Just as CO2 is removed from blood in the lungs, nitrogenous wastes like urea or uric acid are removed from blood in the kidneys. The basic filtration unit in the kidneys, like in the lungs, is a cluster of very thin-walled blood capillaries. In the lungs, alveoli with walls rich in blood vessels provide a surface for gas exchange. In the kidneys, nephrons filter blood through Bowman's capsule and reabsorb useful substances.

subject: Biology
question_english: What methods do plants use to get rid of excretory products?
question_hinglish: Plants excretory products se chhutkara paane ke liye kaun se methods use karte hain?
answer_english:
1. Oxygen from photosynthesis and carbon dioxide are removed through stomata.
2. Excess water is removed by transpiration.
3. Many wastes are stored in cellular vacuoles.
4. Wastes may be stored in leaves that fall off.
5. Other wastes are stored as resins and gums, especially in old xylem.
6. Some wastes are excreted into the surrounding soil.

question_english: Why can oxygen be thought of as a waste product of plants?
question_hinglish: Oxygen ko plants ka waste product kyun maana ja sakta hai?

subject: Biology
question_english: Why do we associate visible movement with life, and why must such movement be controlled?
question_hinglish: Hum visible movement ko life se kyun jodte hain, aur aisi movement controlled kyun honi chahiye?
answer_english: We think of movement as a response to a change in the environment and as an attempt by organisms to use these changes to their advantage. Each kind of change evokes an appropriate movement; for example, we whisper rather than shout to talk to friends in class. So movement must be connected to recognising events and making only the correct response, which requires systems of control and coordination.

subject: Biology
question_english: What is the need for a system of control and coordination in an organism?
question_hinglish: Kisi organism mein control aur coordination ke system ki zaroorat kyun hai?
answer_english: Organisms must respond to changes in their environment with appropriate, controlled movements, and each kind of change needs a specific response. Control and coordination systems recognise events in the environment and trigger only the correct response, and they integrate the activities of different tissues, for example to protect the body when touching a hot object.
answer_hinglish: Organisms ko environment ke changes pe appropriate, controlled movements se respond karna hota hai, aur har change ke liye ek specific response chahiye. Control aur coordination systems environment ke events pehchaante hain aur sirf sahi response trigger karte hain, aur alag tissues ki activities ko integrate karte hain, jaise garam cheez chhoone pe body ko bachana.
ncert_context: When bright light falls on our eyes or we touch a hot object, we detect the change and respond with movement to protect ourselves. All such movement in response to the environment is carefully controlled, and each change evokes an appropriate response. Such controlled movement must be connected to recognising events, followed by only the correct movement. Living organisms must therefore use specialised tissues providing control and coordination.

subject: Biology
question_english: Describe how a nerve impulse travels from one neuron to the next.
question_hinglish: Nerve impulse ek neuron se agle neuron tak kaise travel karta hai, describe karo.
answer_english: Information acquired at the dendritic tip of a nerve cell sets off a chemical reaction that creates an electrical impulse. The impulse travels from the dendrite to the cell body and then along the axon to its end. There, it sets off the release of chemicals, which cross the gap called the synapse and start a similar electrical impulse in a dendrite of the next neuron.
answer_hinglish: Nerve cell ke dendritic tip pe mili information ek chemical reaction shuru karti hai jisse electrical impulse banta hai. Yeh impulse dendrite se cell body tak, phir axon ke along uske end tak jaata hai. Wahan yeh kuch chemicals release karata hai, jo synapse naam ka gap paar karke agle neuron ki dendrite mein waisa hi electrical impulse shuru kar dete hain.

These chemicals cross the gap, or synapse, and start a similar electrical impulse in a dendrite of the next neuron.

question_english: What is a reflex action? Give examples.
question_hinglish: Reflex action kya hai? Examples do.

subject: Biology
question_english: What is a reflex arc and why is it needed?
question_hinglish: Reflex arc kya hai aur iski zaroorat kyun hai?
answer_english: A reflex arc is a simple connection between the nerves that detect a stimulus (input) and the nerves that move muscles (output), so that detection and response are completed quickly without thinking. It is needed because thinking involves complex interactions of many neurons in the brain and takes too long; for example, we might get burnt before deciding to move our hand from a hot object.
answer_hinglish: Reflex arc stimulus detect karne wali nerves (input) aur muscles ko move karne wali nerves (output) ke beech ek simple connection hai, jisse bina soche detection aur response jaldi ho jaata hai. Iski zaroorat isliye hai kyunki sochne mein brain ke kai neurons ke complex interactions hote hain aur bahut time lagta hai; jaise garam cheez se haath hatane ka decide karne se pehle hi hum jal sakte hain.
ncert_context: If we had to think consciously about pain before moving our hand from a flame, it might take enough time for us to get burnt, because thinking involves complicated interactions of many nerve impulses in the brain. Instead, if nerves that detect heat were connected to nerves that move muscles in a simpler way, detecting the input and responding with an output could be completed quickly. Such a connection is called a reflex arc.

subject: Biology
question_english: Where are reflex arcs formed, and why there?
question_hinglish: Reflex arcs kahan bante hain, aur wahin kyun?
answer_english: Reflex arcs are formed in the spinal cord. Nerves from all over the body meet in a bundle in the spinal cord on their way to the brain, so this is the point where the input and output nerves first meet each other, which is the best place for the connection. The information input also goes on to reach the brain.
answer_hinglish: Reflex arcs spinal cord mein bante hain. Body ke har hisse ki nerves brain tak jaate hue spinal cord mein ek bundle mein milti hain, toh yahi woh jagah hai jahan input aur output nerves pehli baar milti hain, isliye connection ke liye yeh best jagah hai. Information input phir bhi brain tak pahunchta hai.

question_english: Why have reflex arcs evolved in animals, and why do they continue to be useful even in animals that can think?
question_hinglish: Animals mein reflex arcs kyun evolve hue, aur sochne wale animals mein bhi yeh useful kyun hain?

subject: Biology
question_english: What is the difference between a reflex action and walking?
question_hinglish: Reflex action aur walking mein kya difference hai?
answer_english: A reflex action is a sudden response to a stimulus that happens without thinking, through a reflex arc in the spinal cord. Walking is a voluntary action that we decide to do; it is controlled by the brain, and its precision and balance are maintained by the cerebellum.
answer_hinglish: Reflex action stimulus ka achanak, bina soche hone wala response hai, jo spinal cord ke reflex arc se hota hai. Walking ek voluntary action hai jo hum decide karke karte hain; ise brain control karta hai, aur iski precision aur balance cerebellum maintain karta hai.
ncert_context: Reflex actions are sudden responses done without thinking, using reflex arcs formed in the spinal cord. Voluntary actions, such as writing, talking or moving a chair, are based on deciding what to do next, so the brain sends messages to muscles. Activities like walking in a straight line, riding a bicycle or picking up a pencil are possible due to the cerebellum, which is responsible for the precision of voluntary actions and maintaining posture and balance.

subject: Biology
question_english: How are involuntary actions different from reflex actions?
question_hinglish: Involuntary actions reflex actions se kaise alag hain?
answer_english: Reflex actions are sudden responses to a stimulus, such as pulling the hand away from a flame or the change in pupil size, made through reflex arcs in the spinal cord. ncert_context: Between simple reflex actions, like change in pupil size, and thought-out actions, like moving a chair, there is another set of muscle movements over which we have no thinking control. question_english: Trace the sequence of events when a bright light is focussed on your eyes.
question_hinglish: Jab aankhon pe tez roshni padti hai toh events ka sequence trace karo.

question_english: What constitutes the central nervous system and the peripheral nervous system?
question_hinglish: Central nervous system aur peripheral nervous system kis se bane hain?
answer_english: The brain and spinal cord constitute the central nervous system, which receives information from all parts of the body and integrates it. question_english: What are voluntary actions? How does the brain carry them out?

subject: Biology
question_english: Describe the functions of the fore-brain.
question_hinglish: Fore-brain ke functions describe karo.
answer_english: The fore-brain is the main thinking part of the brain. It has regions that receive sensory impulses, with separate areas for hearing, smell, sight and so on. Association areas interpret this information along with stored information, a decision is made, and it is passed to motor areas that control voluntary muscles. A separate part of the fore-brain has the centre associated with hunger, which gives the sensation of feeling full.

Fore-brain ke ek alag part mein hunger se juda centre hai jisse pet bhara hone ka ehsaas hota hai.

question_english: Which signals will be disrupted in case of a spinal cord injury?

subject: Biology
question_english: What are the two types of movement shown by plants? Give examples.
question_hinglish: Plants kaun se do types ki movement dikhate hain? Examples do.
answer_english: Plants show movement independent of growth, such as the leaves of the sensitive plant (chhui-mui) folding and drooping quickly when touched, and movement dependent on growth, such as the directional movement of a seedling, where the root goes down and the stem comes up. If the seedling is prevented from growing, it shows no movement.
answer_hinglish: Plants ek growth se independent movement dikhate hain, jaise chhui-mui ki leaves chhoone pe turant mud kar jhuk jaati hain, aur ek growth pe dependent movement, jaise seedling ki directional movement, jisme root neeche aur stem upar jaata hai. Agar seedling ko grow karne se roka jaaye toh koi movement nahi hoti.
ncert_context: Plants have neither a nervous system nor muscles, yet they respond to stimuli. When we touch the leaves of a chhui-mui, the sensitive or touch-me-not plant of the Mimosa family, they fold up and droop very quickly, with no growth involved. When a seed germinates, the root goes down and the stem comes up; this directional movement is caused by growth, and if growth is prevented, there is no movement.

question_english: How do tendrils help a pea plant climb a support?

subject: Biology
question_english: What are tropic movements? Explain phototropism.
question_hinglish: Tropic movements kya hote hain? Phototropism explain karo.
answer_english: Tropic movements are directional growth movements of plant parts in response to environmental triggers such as light or gravity, either towards or away from the stimulus. In phototropism, shoots respond by bending towards light, while roots respond by bending away from it.
answer_hinglish: Tropic movements light ya gravity jaise environmental triggers ke response mein plant parts ki directional growth movements hain, jo stimulus ki taraf ya usse door ho sakti hain. Phototropism mein shoots light ki taraf mudte hain, jabki roots light se door mudte hain.

subject: Biology
question_english: In Activity 6.2, germinated bean seeds on a flask in a box open towards light show shoots bending towards light and roots away. What happens when the flask is turned around, and what can be concluded?
question_hinglish: Activity 6.2 mein light ki taraf khule box mein flask pe rakhe germinated bean seeds ke shoots light ki taraf aur roots door mudte hain. Flask ghumane pe kya hota hai, aur isse kya conclude hota hai?
answer_english: When the flask is turned so that shoots face away from light, the old parts of the shoot and root do not change direction, but the new growth of the shoots bends towards light and the new growth of the roots bends away from it. This shows that shoots are positively and roots negatively phototropic, and that tropic movement happens through growth.
answer_hinglish: Jab flask ko aise ghumaya jaata hai ki shoots light se door hon, toh shoot aur root ke purane parts direction nahi badalte, lekin shoots ki nayi growth light ki taraf aur roots ki nayi growth light se door mudti hai. Isse pata chalta hai ki shoots light ki taraf aur roots light se door phototropic hain, aur tropic movement growth se hoti hai.
ncert_context: In Activity 6.2, a conical flask filled with water is covered with wire mesh holding two or three freshly germinated bean seeds, and kept in a cardboard box open on one side facing a window. After two or three days, shoots bend towards light and roots away. The flask is then turned so shoots face away from light, and after a few days the old parts and the new growth of shoot and root are compared.

subject: Biology
question_english: What are the limitations of electrical impulses for communication, and why do multicellular organisms also use chemical communication?
question_hinglish: Communication ke liye electrical impulses ki kya limitations hain, aur multicellular organisms chemical communication bhi kyun use karte hain?
answer_english: Electrical impulses reach only cells connected by nervous tissue, not every cell, and a cell needs time to reset before generating a new impulse, so it cannot transmit impulses continually. Chemical communication, where cells release compounds that diffuse and are detected by other cells, is slower but can reach all cells regardless of nervous connections and can be done steadily and persistently.
answer_hinglish: Electrical impulses sirf un cells tak pahunchte hain jo nervous tissue se jude hain, har cell tak nahi, aur cell ko naya impulse banane se pehle reset hone mein time lagta hai, toh woh lagataar impulses nahi bhej sakta. Chemical communication, jisme cells compounds release karte hain jo diffuse hokar doosre cells detect karte hain, slow hai lekin nervous connections ke bina saare cells tak pahunch sakta hai aur steadily chal sakta hai.
ncert_context: Fast responses need rapid information transfer, and electrical impulses are excellent for this. But they reach only those cells connected by nervous tissue, and once a cell generates an impulse it takes time to reset, so cells cannot continually create impulses. Most multicellular organisms therefore also use chemical communication: stimulated cells release a compound that diffuses around, and cells with special surface molecules detect it. This is slower but reaches all cells.

subject: Biology
question_english: What are plant hormones?
question_hinglish: Plant hormones kya hote hain?
answer_english: Plant hormones are chemical compounds that help coordinate growth, development and responses to the environment in plants. They are synthesised at places away from where they act and simply diffuse to the area of action.
answer_hinglish: Plant hormones aise chemical compounds hain jo plants mein growth, development aur environment ke responses ko coordinate karte hain. Yeh jahan kaam karte hain usse door bante hain aur diffuse hokar kaam wali jagah tak pahunchte hain.
ncert_context: Hormones are compounds used by multicellular organisms for control and coordination, and they show a great deal of diversity. Different plant hormones help to coordinate growth, development and responses to the environment. They are synthesised at places away from where they act and simply diffuse to the area of action. Examples include auxins, gibberellins, cytokinins and abscisic acid.

subject: Biology
question_english: Name the plant hormones that promote growth and the one that inhibits growth, with their functions.
question_hinglish: Growth promote karne wale aur growth rokne wale plant hormones ke naam aur unke functions batao.
answer_english: Growth-promoting hormones: auxin helps cells grow longer and causes bending towards light; gibberellins help in the growth of the stem; cytokinins promote cell division and are found in greater concentration in areas of rapid cell division, such as fruits and seeds. subject: Biology
question_english: How does adrenaline prepare the body to deal with a scary situation?
question_hinglish: Adrenaline body ko daravni situation se deal karne ke liye kaise taiyaar karta hai?
answer_english: Adrenaline is secreted by the adrenal glands directly into the blood and carried to different parts of the body. It makes the heart beat faster, supplying more oxygen to muscles; it reduces blood to the digestive system and skin by contracting muscles around small arteries, diverting blood to skeletal muscles; and it increases the breathing rate through contractions of the diaphragm and rib muscles.

subject: Biology
question_english: Why would electrical impulses alone not be enough to prepare a squirrel's body for fighting or running away?
question_hinglish: Squirrel ki body ko ladne ya bhaagne ke liye taiyaar karne ke liye sirf electrical impulses kaafi kyun nahi honge?
answer_english: Fighting or running uses many different tissue types whose activities must be integrated, and both need common preparations throughout the body. subject: Biology
question_english: What is the role of growth hormone, and what happens if it is deficient in childhood?
question_hinglish: Growth hormone ka kya role hai, aur bachpan mein iski kami se kya hota hai?
answer_english: Growth hormone, secreted by the pituitary gland, regulates growth and development of the body. If there is a deficiency of this hormone in childhood, it leads to dwarfism. answer_hinglish: Pituitary gland se nikalne wala growth hormone body ki growth aur development regulate karta hai. Bachpan mein iski kami se dwarfism hota hai. subject: Biology
question_english: Compare and contrast nervous and hormonal mechanisms for control and coordination in animals.
question_hinglish: Animals mein control aur coordination ke nervous aur hormonal mechanisms ko compare karo.
answer_english: The nervous mechanism uses electrical impulses through nerve cells; it is fast but reaches only cells connected by nervous tissue, and cells need time to reset between impulses. The hormonal mechanism uses chemicals secreted by endocrine glands into the blood; it is slower but reaches all cells of the body and can act steadily and persistently. Both work together, for example in preparing for an emergency.
answer_hinglish: Nervous mechanism nerve cells ke through electrical impulses use karta hai; yeh fast hai lekin sirf nervous tissue se jude cells tak pahunchta hai, aur cells ko impulses ke beech reset hone mein time lagta hai. Hormonal mechanism endocrine glands se blood mein secrete hue chemicals use karta hai; yeh slow hai lekin body ke saare cells tak pahunchta hai aur steadily kaam kar sakta hai. Dono saath mein kaam karte hain, jaise emergency ki taiyari mein.
ncert_context: The nervous system uses electrical impulses to transmit messages; these are fast but reach only cells connected by nervous tissue, and cells cannot continually create impulses. Hormones are chemical messengers; animal hormones such as adrenaline are secreted by endocrine glands into the blood and carried to all parts of the body. Chemical communication is slower but reaches all cells and acts persistently. The endocrine system is a second way of control and coordination.

The blood carries them to target organs or tissues, where they bring about specific effects; the endocrine system is a second way of control and coordination, and the amount of hormone released is regulated by feedback mechanisms.
answer_hinglish: Animals mein chemical coordination endocrine glands se seedha blood mein secrete hone wale hormones se hota hai. Blood inhe target organs ya tissues tak le jaata hai, jahan yeh specific effects laate hain; endocrine system control aur coordination ka doosra tarika hai, aur hormone ki amount feedback mechanisms se regulate hoti hai.
ncert_context: Animal hormones are part of the endocrine system, which constitutes a second way of control and coordination in our body. For example, adrenaline is secreted from the adrenal glands directly into the blood and carried to different parts of the body, acting on target organs such as the heart. Hormones produced in one part of an organism move to another part to achieve the desired effect, and a feedback mechanism regulates their action.

subject: Biology
question_english: Animals do not grow in a particular direction in response to light or gravity. How then do hormones help in coordinated growth in animals?
question_hinglish: Animals light ya gravity ke response mein kisi particular direction mein grow nahi karte. Toh hormones animals mein coordinated growth mein kaise help karte hain?

subject: Biology
question_english: Reproduction is not necessary to keep an individual organism alive. Why, then, do we notice organisms mainly because they reproduce?
question_hinglish: Reproduction kisi individual organism ko zinda rakhne ke liye zaroori nahi hai. Phir hum organisms ko mainly reproduction ki wajah se hi kyun notice karte hain?
answer_english: Unlike nutrition, respiration or excretion, reproduction is not needed to maintain an individual's life, and it uses a lot of energy. It is the large numbers of organisms of a single species, produced by reproduction, that bring them to our notice.

subject: Biology
question_english: Why is DNA copying an essential part of reproduction?
question_hinglish: Reproduction mein DNA copying ek zaroori part kyun hai?
answer_english: Organisms look similar because their body designs are similar, and the blueprints for body design are in the DNA, which is the information source for making proteins. If the information changes, different proteins and altered body designs result. So reproduction at its most basic level involves making copies of DNA, the blueprint of body design.
answer_hinglish: Organisms isliye similar dikhte hain kyunki unke body designs similar hote hain, aur body design ke blueprints DNA mein hote hain, jo proteins banane ka information source hai. Agar information badle toh alag proteins aur badla hua body design banega. Isliye reproduction ka sabse basic step DNA, yaani body design ke blueprint, ki copies banana hai.
ncert_context: Organisms look similar because their body designs are similar, and for this, the blueprints for these designs should be similar. So reproduction at its most basic level involves making copies of the blueprints of body design. The DNA in the cell nucleus is the information source for making proteins. If the information is changed, different proteins will be made, leading to altered body designs. Therefore, a basic event in reproduction is the creation of a DNA copy.

subject: Biology
question_english: Why must DNA copying be accompanied by the creation of additional cellular apparatus?
question_hinglish: DNA copying ke saath additional cellular apparatus banana kyun zaroori hai?
answer_english: If one DNA copy were kept in the original cell and the other simply pushed out, the copy pushed out would have no organised cellular structure to maintain life processes. So DNA copying is accompanied by creating additional cellular apparatus, and the DNA copies then separate, each with its own cellular apparatus, so a cell divides into two cells.
answer_hinglish: Agar ek DNA copy original cell mein rakh kar doosri ko bas bahar dhakel diya jaaye, toh bahar gayi copy ke paas life processes maintain karne ke liye koi organised cellular structure nahi hoga. Isliye DNA copying ke saath extra cellular apparatus banta hai, aur phir DNA copies apne-apne apparatus ke saath alag hoti hain, yaani ek cell do cells mein divide hota hai.
ncert_context: Cells use chemical reactions to build copies of their DNA, creating two copies in a reproducing cell that need to be separated. Keeping one copy in the original cell and simply pushing the other out would not work, because the copy pushed out would not have any organised cellular structure for maintaining life processes. Therefore, DNA copying is accompanied by the creation of additional cellular apparatus, and the copies separate, each with its own apparatus.

subject: Biology
question_english: Why are the two cells formed after DNA copying similar but not absolutely identical?
question_hinglish: DNA copying ke baad bane do cells similar kyun hote hain lekin bilkul identical kyun nahi?
answer_english: No bio-chemical reaction is absolutely reliable, so the process of copying DNA has some variations each time. As a result, the DNA copies are similar but may not be identical to the original. Some variations are so drastic that the new cell dies, but many others are not, so the surviving cells are similar to but subtly different from each other.
answer_hinglish: Koi bhi bio-chemical reaction bilkul reliable nahi hoti, isliye DNA copying mein har baar kuch variations aate hain. Isse DNA copies original jaisi toh hoti hain par identical nahi. Kuch variations itne drastic hote hain ki naya cell mar jaata hai, lekin kai nahi hote, isliye bache hue cells ek-doosre jaise hote hain par thode alag.
ncert_context: Whether the two cells formed are identical depends on how accurately the copying reactions occur. No bio-chemical reaction is absolutely reliable, so DNA copying will have some variations each time. The DNA copies generated will be similar but may not be identical to the original. Some variations might be so drastic that the new DNA copy cannot work with the inherited cellular apparatus, and the cell dies. Other variations do not lead to such drastic outcomes.

question_english: Why is variation beneficial to the species but not necessarily to the individual?
question_hinglish: Variation species ke liye faydemand kyun hai lekin har individual ke liye zaroori nahi?
answer_english: Niches can change drastically due to reasons like rising temperatures or changing water levels, and a population suited only to the old niche could be wiped out. subject: Biology
question_english: How does binary fission differ from multiple fission? Give examples.
question_hinglish: Binary fission multiple fission se kaise alag hai? Examples do.
answer_english: In binary fission, a unicellular organism splits into two daughter cells; many bacteria and protozoa split into two equal halves, Amoeba can split in any plane, and Leishmania splits in a definite orientation in relation to its whip-like structure. In multiple fission, an organism divides into many daughter cells simultaneously, as in the malarial parasite Plasmodium.
answer_hinglish: Binary fission mein unicellular organism do daughter cells mein bat jaata hai; kai bacteria aur protozoa do barabar halves mein batte hain, Amoeba kisi bhi plane mein bat sakta hai, aur Leishmania apne whip jaise structure ke hisaab se ek definite orientation mein batta hai. Multiple fission mein organism ek saath kai daughter cells mein divide hota hai, jaise malarial parasite Plasmodium mein.

subject: Biology
question_english: What is regeneration? How is it carried out?
question_hinglish: Regeneration kya hai? Yeh kaise hota hai?
answer_english: Regeneration is the ability of fully differentiated organisms like Hydra and Planaria to give rise to new organisms from body parts; if cut into pieces, each piece grows into a complete organism. It is carried out by specialised cells that proliferate to form a mass of cells, from which different cells change into various cell types and tissues in an organised sequence called development.

subject: Biology
question_english: Describe the process of tissue culture and its advantages.
question_hinglish: Tissue culture ka process aur iske advantages describe karo.
answer_english: In tissue culture, tissue or cells are removed from the growing tip of a plant and placed in an artificial medium, where they divide rapidly to form a callus. The callus is transferred to another medium with hormones for growth and differentiation, and the plantlets are then placed in soil to grow into mature plants. Many plants can be grown from one parent in disease-free conditions; it is commonly used for ornamental plants.
answer_hinglish: Tissue culture mein plant ki growing tip se tissue ya cells nikal kar artificial medium mein rakhe jaate hain, jahan woh tezi se divide hokar callus banate hain. Callus ko hormones wale doosre medium mein rakha jaata hai taaki growth aur differentiation ho, aur phir plantlets ko soil mein lagaya jaata hai taaki woh mature plants banein. Ek parent se disease-free conditions mein kai plants ugaye ja sakte hain; yeh mostly ornamental plants ke liye use hota hai.

Intent Type: explain_concept
Answer the question in English using only the given context.

In tissue culture, tissue or cells are removed from the growing tip of a plant and placed in an artificial medium, where they divide rapidly to form a callus. The callus is transferred to another medium with hormones for growth and differentiation, and the plantlets are then placed in soil to grow into mature plants. Many plants can be grown from one parent in disease-free conditions; it is commonly used for ornamental plants.

question_english: How does Rhizopus (bread mould) reproduce?
question_hinglish: Rhizopus (bread mould) kaise reproduce karta hai?
answer_english: Rhizopus reproduces by spore formation. The spores have thick walls that protect them until they reach a moist surface and begin to grow.

subject: Biology
question_english: How are the modes of reproduction different in unicellular and multicellular organisms?
question_hinglish: Unicellular aur multicellular organisms mein reproduction ke modes kaise alag hain?
answer_english: In unicellular organisms, cell division or fission itself creates new individuals, by binary fission, multiple fission or budding. Multicellular organisms with simple bodies may use fragmentation, regeneration or budding, but complex multicellular organisms have specialised tissues and organs, so they use more complex methods in which reproduction is the function of a specific cell type, such as sexual reproduction with germ-cells.
answer_hinglish: Unicellular organisms mein cell division ya fission se hi naye individuals bante hain, binary fission, multiple fission ya budding se. Simple body wale multicellular organisms fragmentation, regeneration ya budding use kar sakte hain, lekin complex multicellular organisms mein specialised tissues aur organs hote hain, isliye woh complex methods use karte hain jisme reproduction ek specific cell type ka kaam hota hai, jaise germ-cells se sexual reproduction.
ncert_context: For unicellular organisms, cell division or fission leads to new individuals; bacteria and protozoa split by binary fission, Plasmodium by multiple fission and yeast by budding. Multicellular organisms with simple organisation may use fragmentation, like Spirogyra, or regeneration and budding, like Hydra. Complex multicellular organisms cannot divide cell by cell, so reproduction is the function of a specific cell type, and many use sexual reproduction.

subject: Biology
question_english: How does sexual reproduction speed up the generation of variation?
question_hinglish: Sexual reproduction variation banne ki speed kaise badhata hai?
answer_english: DNA copying is precise enough that generating variation by copying errors alone is slow, and making it less accurate would produce many non-working copies. Different individuals carry different patterns of accumulated variations, all of which are not harmful since they are in living individuals. Sexual reproduction combines DNA from two different individuals, creating new, novel combinations of variants.
answer_hinglish: DNA copying itni precise hai ki sirf copying errors se variation dheere-dheere banta hai, aur ise kam accurate banane se kai copies kaam nahi karengi. Alag individuals mein jama hue variations ke alag patterns hote hain, jo harmful nahi hote kyunki woh living individuals mein hain. Sexual reproduction do alag individuals ke DNA ko combine karta hai, jisse variants ke naye, novel combinations bante hain.
ncert_context: DNA copying errors are a source of variation, and variations ensure survival of the species. While DNA copying is not absolutely accurate, it is precise enough to make generating variation slow; less accuracy would make many copies unable to work. Two individuals in a population have different patterns of accumulated variations, and since these are in living individuals, they have no really bad effects. Combining variations from two individuals creates new combinations, which sexual reproduction does.

subject: Biology
question_english: What problem arises if each generation combines DNA from two individuals, and how is it solved?
question_hinglish: Agar har generation do individuals ka DNA combine kare toh kya problem aayegi, aur yeh kaise solve hoti hai?
answer_english: If each new generation combined full DNA copies from two individuals, each generation would have twice the DNA of the previous one, which would disturb the control of the cellular apparatus by DNA. Many multicellular organisms solve this with special lineages of cells in specialised organs that have only half the chromosomes and DNA, formed by meiosis, so the original number is restored when two germ-cells combine.
answer_hinglish: Agar har generation do individuals ki poori DNA copies combine kare, toh har generation mein pichhli se double DNA hoga, jo DNA ke cellular apparatus pe control ko bigaad dega. Kai multicellular organisms yeh specialised organs mein aise cells se solve karte hain jinme aadhe chromosomes aur aadha DNA hota hai, jo meiosis se bante hain, taaki do germ-cells milne pe original number wapas aa jaaye.
ncert_context: If each new generation is the combination of DNA copies from two pre-existing individuals, each generation would have twice the DNA of the previous one, likely messing up the control of the cellular apparatus by DNA. Many multicellular organisms solve this by having special lineages of cells in specialised organs with only half the number of chromosomes and half the DNA, produced by meiosis. When these germ-cells combine, the chromosome number and DNA content are re-established.

subject: Biology
question_english: Why are male and female gametes different in complex organisms?
question_hinglish: Complex organisms mein male aur female gametes alag kyun hote hain?
answer_english: For the zygote to grow into an organism with highly specialised tissues and organs, it needs sufficient stores of energy. In very simple organisms, the two germ-cells may be similar, but as body designs become complex, germ-cells specialise: one is large and contains food stores, called the female gamete, while the other is smaller and motile, called the male gamete.
answer_hinglish: Zygote ko highly specialised tissues aur organs wale organism mein develop hone ke liye kaafi energy store chahiye. Bahut simple organisms mein dono germ-cells similar ho sakte hain, lekin body designs complex hone pe germ-cells specialise ho jaate hain: ek bada hota hai aur usme food stores hote hain, jise female gamete kehte hain, aur doosra chhota aur motile hota hai, jise male gamete kehte hain.
ncert_context: If the zygote is to grow and develop into an organism with highly specialised tissues and organs, it must have sufficient stores of energy. In very simple organisms, the two germ-cells are not very different or may even be similar. But as body designs become more complex, the germ-cells also specialise. One germ-cell is large and contains food stores, while the other is smaller and likely to be motile. The motile one is called the male gamete, and the food-storing one the female gamete.

question_english: What are the advantages of sexual reproduction over asexual reproduction?

subject: Biology
question_english: How is the process of pollination different from fertilisation?
question_hinglish: Pollination ka process fertilisation se kaise alag hai?
answer_english: Pollination is the transfer of pollen from the stamen to the stigma, either within the same flower (self-pollination) or from one flower to another (cross-pollination), by agents like wind, water or animals. Fertilisation is the fusion of the male germ-cell from the pollen grain with the female gamete in the ovule, which forms the zygote.
answer_hinglish: Pollination stamen se stigma tak pollen ka transfer hai, ya toh usi flower mein (self-pollination) ya ek flower se doosre mein (cross-pollination), jo wind, water ya animals jaise agents se hota hai. Fertilisation pollen grain ke male germ-cell ka ovule ke female gamete ke saath fusion hai, jisse zygote banta hai.
ncert_context: The male germ-cell produced by the pollen grain fuses with the female gamete present in the ovule; this fusion is fertilisation and gives the zygote. For this, pollen must be transferred from the stamen to the stigma. Transfer in the same flower is self-pollination, while transfer from one flower to another is cross-pollination, achieved by agents like wind, water or animals. A pollen tube then grows through the style to reach the ovary.

subject: Biology
question_english: How are the changes during puberty, such as new hair growth patterns, linked to reproduction?
question_hinglish: Puberty ke changes, jaise baal ugne ke naye patterns, reproduction se kaise jude hain?
answer_english: Sexual reproduction requires germ-cells from two individuals to join. In animals that mate, their state of sexual maturity must be identifiable by others, and changes like new hair-growth patterns signal that sexual maturation is taking place. Special organs are needed for the transfer of germ-cells, and in humans, the female reproductive organs and breasts mature to carry and later breast-feed a baby.
answer_hinglish: Sexual reproduction mein do individuals ke germ-cells ka milna zaroori hai. Mate karne wale animals mein sexual maturity doosron ko pehchaan mein aani chahiye, aur baal ugne ke naye patterns jaise changes signal hain ki sexual maturation ho raha hai. Germ-cells ke transfer ke liye special organs chahiye, aur humans mein female reproductive organs aur breasts mature hote hain taaki baby ko carry aur baad mein breast-feed kiya ja sake.
ncert_context: Sexual reproduction means germ-cells from two individuals must join, either by external release, as in flowering plants, or by internal transfer, as in many animals. Transfer of germ-cells needs special organs, and in mammals like humans, the baby is carried in the mother's body and later breast-fed.

subject: Biology
question_english: What are the functions performed by the testis in human beings?
question_hinglish: Humans mein testis kaun se functions karte hain?
answer_english: The testes form the male germ-cells, the sperms. They also secrete the hormone testosterone, which regulates the formation of sperms and brings about changes in appearance seen in boys at puberty.
answer_hinglish: Testes male germ-cells, yaani sperms, banate hain. Yeh testosterone hormone bhi secrete karte hain, jo sperms ke banne ko regulate karta hai aur puberty mein ladkon ki appearance mein changes laata hai.
ncert_context: The formation of germ-cells or sperms takes place in the testes. These are located outside the abdominal cavity in the scrotum, because sperm formation requires a lower temperature than the normal body temperature. The testes also secrete the hormone testosterone. In addition to regulating the formation of sperms, testosterone brings about changes in appearance seen in boys at the time of puberty.

subject: Biology
question_english: Describe the path of the egg and the events from fertilisation to the formation of a foetus.
question_hinglish: Egg ka raasta aur fertilisation se lekar foetus banne tak ke events describe karo.
answer_english: One egg is produced every month by one of the ovaries and is carried through the oviduct (fallopian tube) towards the uterus. Sperms entering through the vagina travel up to the oviduct, where they may meet the egg. The fertilised egg (zygote) divides to form a ball of cells, the embryo, which is implanted in the lining of the uterus and continues to grow and develop organs to become a foetus.
answer_hinglish: Har mahine ek ovary ek egg banati hai, jo oviduct (fallopian tube) se uterus ki taraf jaata hai. Vagina se aaye sperms oviduct tak jaate hain jahan woh egg se mil sakte hain. Fertilised egg (zygote) divide hokar cells ki ek ball, yaani embryo, banata hai, jo uterus ki lining mein implant hokar grow karta hai aur organs bana kar foetus ban jaata hai.
ncert_context: When a girl is born, the ovaries already contain thousands of immature eggs; at puberty, some start maturing, and one egg is produced every month by one ovary. The egg is carried from the ovary to the womb through a thin oviduct or fallopian tube. Sperms enter through the vagina and travel up to the oviduct, where they may meet the egg. The zygote divides to form an embryo, which implants in the uterine lining and develops into a foetus.

subject: Biology
question_english: How does the embryo get nourishment inside the mother's body?
question_hinglish: Mother ki body ke andar embryo ko nourishment kaise milta hai?
answer_english: The embryo gets nutrition from the mother's blood through a special tissue called the placenta, a disc embedded in the uterine wall. It has villi on the embryo's side and blood spaces on the mother's side surrounding the villi, providing a large surface area for glucose and oxygen to pass from mother to embryo. Wastes from the embryo are removed into the mother's blood through the placenta.
answer_hinglish: Embryo ko mother ke blood se placenta naam ke special tissue ke through nutrition milta hai, jo uterine wall mein embedded ek disc hai. Isme embryo ki side villi hoti hain aur mother ki side villi ke aas-paas blood spaces hote hain, jo mother se embryo tak glucose aur oxygen jaane ke liye bada surface area dete hain. Embryo ke wastes bhi placenta se mother ke blood mein bhej diye jaate hain.

subject: Biology
question_english: Why does menstruation occur?
question_hinglish: Menstruation kyun hota hai?
answer_english: Since the ovary releases one egg every month, the uterus prepares itself every month to receive a fertilised egg, and its lining becomes thick and spongy. If the egg is not fertilised, it lives for about one day, and the lining is no longer needed, so it slowly breaks and comes out through the vagina as blood and mucous. This roughly monthly cycle is menstruation, usually lasting about two to eight days.

subject: Biology
question_english: What are the different methods of contraception?
question_hinglish: Contraception ke alag-alag methods kya hain?
answer_english:
1. Mechanical barriers, such as condoms on the penis or similar coverings in the vagina, stop sperm from reaching the egg.
2. Oral pills change the hormonal balance so that eggs are not released, but may cause side effects.
3. Devices like the loop or copper-T are placed in the uterus, but may cause irritation.
4. Surgical methods block the vas deferens in males or the fallopian tube in females.

1. Mechanical barriers, jaise penis pe condom ya vagina mein similar coverings, sperm ko egg tak pahunchne se rokte hain.
2. Oral pills hormonal balance badal kar eggs release nahi hone deti, lekin side effects ho sakte hain.
3. Loop ya copper-T jaise devices uterus mein lagaye jaate hain, lekin irritation ho sakta hai.
4. Surgical methods males mein vas deferens ya females mein fallopian tube block karte hain.

subject: Biology
question_english: What could be the reasons for adopting contraceptive methods?
question_hinglish: Contraceptive methods apnane ke kya reasons ho sakte hain?
answer_english: Pregnancy makes major demands on a woman's body and mind, and if she is not ready, her health will be adversely affected, so contraception helps avoid unwanted pregnancy. Some methods, like condoms, also reduce the transmission of sexually transmitted diseases. Contraception also helps control the size of a population, since an expanding population makes it harder to improve everyone's standard of living.

Contraception population size control karne mein bhi help karta hai, kyunki badhti population mein sabka standard of living improve karna mushkil hota hai.

subject: Biology
question_english: Why do we find very little variation among sugarcane plants in a field but distinct variations among human beings?
question_hinglish: Sugarcane ke khet ke plants mein bahut kam variation kyun dikhta hai lekin humans mein clear variations kyun dikhte hain?
answer_english: Sugarcane is grown by vegetative propagation, an asexual method, so the plants show very little variation, arising only from minor inaccuracies in DNA copying. Human beings reproduce sexually, which combines DNA from two individuals and maximises the number of successful variations, so quite distinct variations are visible among individuals.
answer_hinglish: Sugarcane vegetative propagation se ugaya jaata hai, jo asexual method hai, isliye plants mein bahut kam variation hota hai jo sirf DNA copying ki chhoti galtiyon se aata hai. Humans sexually reproduce karte hain, jisme do individuals ka DNA combine hota hai aur successful variations maximum hote hain, isliye individuals mein clear variations dikhte hain.
ncert_context: Reproductive processes give rise to new individuals that are similar but subtly different. Some variation is produced even during asexual reproduction, but the number of successful variations is maximised by sexual reproduction. If we observe a field of sugarcane, we find very little variation among individual plants. But in many animals, including human beings, which reproduce sexually, quite distinct variations are visible among different individuals.

subject: Biology
question_english: How does variation accumulate over generations during reproduction?
question_hinglish: Reproduction ke dauraan generations ke saath variation kaise jama hota hai?
answer_english: Inheritance gives the next generation a common basic body design along with subtle changes. When this generation reproduces, the second generation has the differences inherited from the first, plus newly created differences. In asexual reproduction, like bacteria dividing, differences are very minor, from small inaccuracies in DNA copying, but sexual reproduction generates much greater diversity.
answer_hinglish: Inheritance se agli generation ko common basic body design ke saath kuch chhote changes milte hain. Jab yeh generation reproduce karti hai, toh doosri generation mein pehli se mile differences aur naye differences dono hote hain. Asexual reproduction mein, jaise bacteria ke divide hone mein, differences bahut chhote hote hain, jo DNA copying ki chhoti galtiyon se aate hain, lekin sexual reproduction kahin zyada diversity banata hai.
ncert_context: Inheritance from the previous generation provides both a common basic body design and subtle changes in it for the next generation. When this new generation reproduces, the second generation will have differences inherited from the first generation as well as newly created differences. If one bacterium divides and the two bacteria divide again, the four bacteria would be very similar, with very minor differences due to small inaccuracies in DNA copying. Sexual reproduction generates even greater diversity.

subject: Biology
question_english: In an asexually reproducing species, trait A exists in 10% of the population and trait B in 60%. Which trait is likely to have arisen earlier?
question_hinglish: Ek asexually reproduce karne wali species mein trait A population ke 10% mein aur trait B 60% mein hai. Kaun sa trait pehle aaya hoga?
answer_english: Trait B is likely to have arisen earlier. In asexual reproduction, a variation that arises is passed on to the offspring of that individual, so the longer a trait has existed, the more individuals in later generations will carry it. A trait found in 60% of the population has had more generations to spread than one found in 10%.
answer_hinglish: Trait B pehle aaya hoga. Asexual reproduction mein jo variation aata hai woh us individual ke offspring mein pass hota rehta hai, toh jo trait jitne lambe time se hai, aage ki generations mein utne zyada individuals mein hoga. 60% wale trait ko phailne ke liye 10% wale se zyada generations mili hain.

subject: Biology
question_english: What is meant by heredity and the rules of heredity?
question_hinglish: Heredity aur rules of heredity ka kya matlab hai?
answer_english: Heredity refers to the inheritance of traits and characteristics from one generation to the next. The rules of heredity determine the process by which traits and characteristics are reliably inherited, so that reproduction generates individuals of similar design.
answer_hinglish: Heredity ka matlab ek generation se agli generation tak traits aur characteristics ka inherit hona hai. Rules of heredity woh process decide karte hain jisse traits aur characteristics reliably inherit hote hain, taaki reproduction se similar design wale individuals bane.
ncert_context: The most obvious outcome of the reproductive process is still the generation of individuals of similar design. The rules of heredity determine the process by which traits and characteristics are reliably inherited. A child bears all the basic features of a human being but does not look exactly like its parents, and human populations show a great deal of variation.

subject: Biology
question_english: A man with blood group A marries a woman with blood group O, and their daughter has blood group O. Is this enough to tell which trait, A or O, is dominant?
question_hinglish: Blood group A wala aadmi blood group O wali aurat se shaadi karta hai, aur unki beti ka blood group O hai. Kya isse pata chal sakta hai ki A ya O mein se kaun sa trait dominant hai?
answer_english: No. The daughter receives one copy from each parent. Her blood group O is possible if O is recessive and the father carries one hidden O copy, but this single family does not rule out other possibilities. We would need data from more crosses, especially to see which group appears when the two copies are different.
answer_hinglish: Nahi. Beti ko har parent se ek copy milti hai. Uska blood group O tab possible hai jab O recessive ho aur father mein ek chhupi hui O copy ho, lekin sirf ek family se baaki possibilities rule out nahi hoti. Hume aur crosses ka data chahiye, khaas kar yeh dekhne ke liye ki do alag copies hone pe kaun sa group dikhta hai.

Dominance is worked out by observing which trait is expressed when the copies differ, across generations.

subject: Biology
question_english: How do genes control traits? Explain with the example of plant height.
question_hinglish: Genes traits ko kaise control karte hain? Plant height ke example se explain karo.
answer_english: Plant height depends on the amount of a growth hormone made. The amount of hormone depends on the efficiency of an enzyme involved in making it, and the enzyme is coded by a gene. If the enzyme works efficiently, a lot of hormone is made and the plant is tall; if the gene has an alteration that makes the enzyme less efficient, less hormone is made and the plant is short. Thus genes control traits.

Is tarah genes traits control karte hain.

subject: Biology
question_english: How is the equal genetic contribution of male and female parents ensured in the progeny?
question_hinglish: Progeny mein male aur female parents ka barabar genetic contribution kaise ensure hota hai?
answer_english: Each cell has two copies of each chromosome, one from each parent. Every germ cell takes only one chromosome from each pair, of either maternal or paternal origin, so it has one gene set. When a male and a female germ cell combine, the progeny gets one copy of each chromosome from each parent, restoring the normal number and ensuring equal contribution.

Jab male aur female germ cell milte hain, toh progeny ko har parent se har chromosome ki ek copy milti hai, normal number wapas aa jaata hai aur contribution barabar hota hai.

When two germ cells combine, the normal chromosome number is restored.

subject: Biology
question_english: Why must each gene set be present as separate chromosomes rather than as a single long thread of DNA for independent inheritance to occur?
question_hinglish: Independent inheritance ke liye har gene set ek lambe DNA thread ki jagah alag-alag chromosomes ke roop mein kyun hona chahiye?
answer_english: If progeny inherited a single whole gene set from each parent as one long DNA thread, characteristics like seed shape and seed colour would be linked and could not be inherited independently. Because each gene set is present as separate, independent pieces called chromosomes, and each germ cell takes one chromosome of each pair at random, traits on different chromosomes can recombine independently.
answer_hinglish: Agar progeny ko har parent se ek poora gene set ek lambe DNA thread ke roop mein milta, toh seed shape aur seed colour jaise characteristics linked hote aur independently inherit nahi ho paate. Kyunki har gene set alag, independent pieces, yaani chromosomes, ke roop mein hota hai, aur har germ cell har pair se randomly ek chromosome leta hai, isliye alag chromosomes ke traits independently recombine ho sakte hain.

This is explained by the fact that each gene set is present not as a single long thread of DNA, but as separate independent pieces, each called a chromosome. Every germ cell takes one chromosome from each pair, of maternal or paternal origin.

question_english: Describe the different strategies used by different species for sex determination.
question_hinglish: Alag species sex determination ke liye kaun si alag strategies use karti hain, describe karo.

subject: Biology
question_english: How is the sex of a child determined in human beings?
question_hinglish: Humans mein bachche ka sex kaise determine hota hai?
answer_english: Humans have 22 pairs of chromosomes with a maternal and paternal copy, plus one pair of sex chromosomes. Women have a perfect pair, XX, while men have a mismatched pair, XY. All children inherit an X chromosome from the mother. A child who inherits an X chromosome from the father will be a girl (XX), and one who inherits a Y chromosome from him will be a boy (XY). So the sex is determined by what the child inherits from the father.
answer_hinglish: Humans mein 22 pairs chromosomes ke maternal aur paternal copy hoti hai, aur ek pair sex chromosomes ka hota hai. Women mein perfect pair XX hota hai, jabki men mein mismatched pair XY. Saare bachchon ko mother se X chromosome milta hai. Jis bachche ko father se X milta hai woh ladki (XX) hoti hai, aur jise Y milta hai woh ladka (XY) hota hai. Isliye sex is baat se decide hota hai ki bachche ko father se kya mila.

subject: Biology
question_english: Using the inheritance of X and Y chromosomes, show what fraction of children are expected to be boys and girls.
question_hinglish: X aur Y chromosomes ki inheritance use karke dikhao ki kitne fraction bachche ladke aur kitne ladkiyan honge.
answer_english:
Mother (XX) gives only X; father (XY) gives X or Y.
Possible combinations: X from mother with X from father = XX (girl); X from mother with Y from father = XY (boy).
Each is equally likely, so 1/2 of the children are expected to be girls and 1/2 boys.

question_english: Why does an aquarium need to be cleaned from time to time, while ponds and lakes do not need such cleaning?

subject: Biology
question_english: Explain the 10 percent law of energy flow in an ecosystem.
question_hinglish: Ecosystem mein energy flow ka 10 percent law explain karo.
answer_english: Green plants capture about 1% of the sunlight falling on their leaves and convert it into food energy. When a consumer eats food, a great deal of energy is lost as heat, some is used in digestion and work, and only an average of 10% of the food eaten is turned into its own body and made available to the next level. So about 10% of the organic matter reaches each next trophic level.
answer_hinglish: Green plants unki leaves pe padne wali sunlight ka lagbhag 1% capture karke food energy banate hain. Isliye har agle trophic level tak lagbhag 10% organic matter pahunchta hai.

subject: Biology
question_english: If 10,000 J of energy is available to the producers in a food chain, how much energy will be available to the tertiary consumers, assuming 10% transfer at each step?
question_hinglish: Agar ek food chain mein producers ke paas 10,000 J energy hai, toh har step pe 10% transfer maan ke tertiary consumers ko kitni energy milegi?
answer_english:
Producers (1st level) = 10,000 J.
Primary consumers (2nd level) = 10% of 10,000 = 1,000 J.
Secondary consumers (3rd level) = 10% of 1,000 = 100 J.
Tertiary consumers (4th level) = 10% of 100 = 10 J.
So only 10 J is available to the tertiary consumers.

subject: Biology
question_english: What two things become clear from the energy flow in an ecosystem?
question_hinglish: Ecosystem mein energy flow se kaun si do baatein clear hoti hain?
answer_english: First, the flow of energy is unidirectional: energy captured by autotrophs does not revert to the solar input, and energy passed to herbivores does not come back to autotrophs. Second, the energy available at each trophic level diminishes progressively due to the loss of energy at each level.
answer_hinglish: Pehli, energy ka flow unidirectional hai: autotrophs ki capture ki hui energy wapas solar input mein nahi jaati, aur herbivores ko gayi energy wapas autotrophs ko nahi aati. Doosri, har level pe energy loss ki wajah se har trophic level pe available energy lagataar kam hoti jaati hai.
ncert_context: From the energy flow diagram, two things become clear. Firstly, the flow of energy is unidirectional. The energy captured by the autotrophs does not revert back to the solar input, and the energy which passes to the herbivores does not come back to autotrophs. As it moves progressively through the trophic levels, it is no longer available to the previous level. Secondly, the energy available at each trophic level gets diminished progressively due to loss of energy at each level.

question_english: What will happen if we kill all the organisms in one trophic level?
question_hinglish: Agar hum ek trophic level ke saare organisms ko maar dein toh kya hoga?
answer_english: Organisms at different trophic levels depend on each other. This would disturb the balance of the whole ecosystem.

subject: Biology
question_english: Will the impact of removing all organisms in a trophic level differ for different levels? Can any trophic level be removed without damaging the ecosystem?
question_hinglish: Kya alag-alag trophic levels ke saare organisms hatane ka impact alag hoga? Kya kisi trophic level ko bina ecosystem ko nuksaan pahunchaye hataya ja sakta hai?
answer_english: Yes, the impact differs. Removing producers would be most damaging, since they make the energy from sunlight available to all other organisms, so all consumers would eventually die. subject: Biology
question_english: What is biological magnification? Will its level be different at different trophic levels?
question_hinglish: Biological magnification kya hai? Kya alag trophic levels pe iska level alag hoga?
answer_english: Biological magnification is the progressive accumulation of non-degradable harmful chemicals, such as pesticides, at each trophic level of a food chain. Yes, the level differs: the concentration increases at each higher level, and since human beings occupy the top level, the maximum concentration accumulates in our bodies.
answer_hinglish: Biological magnification food chain ke har trophic level pe pesticides jaise non-degradable harmful chemicals ka lagataar jama hona hai. Haan, level alag hota hai: har upar wale level pe concentration badhti jaati hai, aur kyunki humans sabse upar ke level pe hain, maximum concentration hamari body mein jama hoti hai.
ncert_context: Pesticides and other chemicals used to protect crops are washed into the soil or water bodies. From soil, they are absorbed by plants along with water and minerals, and from water bodies, they are taken up by aquatic plants and animals, entering the food chain. As these chemicals are not degradable, they accumulate progressively at each trophic level. As humans occupy the top level, the maximum concentration accumulates in our bodies. This is biological magnification.

subject: Biology
question_english: How do pesticides enter our food, and why can't they always be removed?
question_hinglish: Pesticides hamare khane mein kaise aate hain, aur unhe hamesha hataya kyun nahi ja sakta?
answer_english: Pesticides used on crops are washed into the soil or water bodies. Plants absorb them from the soil with water and minerals, and aquatic plants and animals take them up from water, so they enter the food chain. That is why food grains, vegetables, fruits and even meat contain varying amounts of pesticide residues, which cannot always be removed by washing or other means.
answer_hinglish: Crops pe use hone wale pesticides soil ya water bodies mein beh jaate hain. Plants unhe soil se paani aur minerals ke saath absorb karte hain, aur aquatic plants aur animals unhe paani se lete hain, toh woh food chain mein aa jaate hain. Isliye food grains, vegetables, fruits aur meat mein bhi pesticide residues hote hain, jo hamesha dhone ya doosre tarikon se nahi hatte.
ncert_context: Several pesticides and chemicals are used to protect crops from diseases and pests. These chemicals are washed down into the soil or into water bodies. From the soil, they are absorbed by plants along with water and minerals, and from water bodies, they are taken up by aquatic plants and animals; this is how they enter the food chain. This is why food grains like wheat and rice, vegetables, fruits and even meat contain pesticide residues that cannot always be removed by washing.

subject: Biology
question_english: What is ozone and how is it formed in the upper atmosphere?
question_hinglish: Ozone kya hai aur upper atmosphere mein yeh kaise banti hai?
answer_english: Ozone (O3) is a molecule formed by three atoms of oxygen. In the upper atmosphere, high-energy UV radiation splits some molecular oxygen (O2) into free oxygen atoms (O), and these atoms combine with molecular oxygen to form ozone: O2 → O + O, then O + O2 → O3.
answer_hinglish: Ozone (O3) oxygen ke teen atoms se bana molecule hai. Upper atmosphere mein high-energy UV radiation kuch molecular oxygen (O2) ko free oxygen atoms (O) mein tod deti hai, aur yeh atoms molecular oxygen se milkar ozone banate hain: O2 → O + O, phir O + O2 → O3.
ncert_context: Ozone is a molecule formed by three atoms of oxygen, while O2, which we normally call oxygen, is essential for aerobic life. Ozone is a deadly poison, but at higher levels of the atmosphere it shields the earth from ultraviolet radiation. Ozone at higher levels is a product of UV radiation acting on the oxygen molecule. Higher energy UV radiation splits some molecular oxygen into free oxygen atoms, which then combine with molecular oxygen to form ozone.

subject: Biology
question_english: Ozone is a deadly poison, so why is the ozone layer important? Why is its damage a cause for concern?
question_hinglish: Ozone ek deadly poison hai, phir ozone layer important kyun hai? Iska damage chinta ki baat kyun hai?
answer_english: At higher levels of the atmosphere, ozone shields the surface of the earth from ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the Sun. So damage to the ozone layer would let more UV radiation reach the earth, harming living organisms and the environment.

subject: Biology
question_english: What has caused the depletion of the ozone layer, and what steps have been taken to limit it?
question_hinglish: Ozone layer ki depletion kis wajah se hui hai, aur ise kam karne ke liye kya steps liye gaye hain?
answer_english: The amount of ozone began to drop sharply in the 1980s, which has been linked to synthetic chemicals called chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), used as refrigerants and in fire extinguishers. In 1987, the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) forged an agreement to freeze CFC production at 1986 levels, and it is now mandatory for manufacturers to make CFC-free refrigerators throughout the world.

question_english: Why were kulhads (clay cups) not a good large-scale alternative to disposable plastic cups in trains? What are the advantages of disposable paper cups?

question_english: True or False: The energy that passes from producers to herbivores can flow back to the producers.
